title: Isolation picker shows only 'Folder' (grayed out) when folder is not git-backed
description:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Unknown

- VS Code Version: main
- OS Version: 

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Create or open a folder that is not a git repository.
2. Open the isolation picker (the UI that lets you choose how to open the workspace/isolation target).
3. Observe that only the "Folder" option is shown and it appears grayed out; the "Worktree" option is not shown and there is no indication why.

Expected behavior:

- The isolation picker should indicate why Worktree is unavailable when the folder is not git-backed. Preferably both options (Folder and Worktree) could be shown, and when the user selects Worktree, VS Code could offer to initialize a git repository in that folder (git init) or provide a clear action to enable worktrees.

Actual behavior:

- Only "Folder" is shown (grayed out) with no explanation, which is confusing for users who expect worktrees to be available.

Proposed fix / suggestion:

- Show both options in the isolation picker. If the folder is not git-backed, either:
  - Disable the Worktree option but show a clear message explaining that a git repository is required and offer an inline action to initialize git in the folder, or
  - Allow selecting Worktree and prompt to initialize a git repository (run `git init`) in that folder so the user can proceed.

Notes:

- This came up during internal testing of a new repository — the folder being new (no git) made the picker behavior confusing. Adding an explanatory message or an init action should improve discoverability and UX.

title: Agents window: editor layout actions missing in single-tab mode
description:
In the Agents window, the editor-area layout controls — **Maximize Editor Area**, **Restore Editor Area**, **Close Editor Area**, **Open in Modal Editor**, and the secondary side bar toggle — disappeared when `workbench.editor.showTabs` was set to `single`.

These actions are contributed to the editor title layout menu, which in single-tab mode is rendered by `SingleEditorTabsControl` — and it returned an empty set of layout actions, so the whole group went missing.

Fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/322908.

title: Agent host: client tool calls in the default chat hang (never resolved)
description:
## Problem

Client-provided tool calls running in a session's **default chat** can hang: the SDK handler's deferred is never resolved, so the agent waits forever on a tool result that already came back.

## Root cause

`ChatToolCallComplete` envelopes are emitted on the chat channel URI, which is formatted as:

```
ahp-chat://<chatId>/<base64(sessionUri)>
```

In `agentSideEffects.ts`, both dispatch paths forwarded that chat URI straight into `IAgent.onClientToolCallComplete(session, ...)`. But every agent keys its `_sessions` map by the raw session id, resolved via `AgentSession.id(uri)` = `uri.path.substring(1)`. For a chat URI that path is the **base64 blob**, not the session GUID, so the default-chat lookup never matched and the completion was silently dropped.

This affected the copilot, claude, and codex agents. Peer (additional, non-default) chats happened to still work because they resolve through a separate `_chatSessions` map keyed by the chat URI.

## Fix

Forward the resolved session URI for the default chat (so `AgentSession.id` yields the GUID), and keep forwarding the chat URI for peer chats. Tracked in [#323302](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/323302).

## Follow-ups to consider

- The footgun is that `onClientToolCallComplete(session, ...)` accepts a URI that is sometimes a session URI and sometimes a chat URI, and each agent re-derives routing. Worth considering a clearer contract or a single shared resolution helper so this can't silently regress.
- Add broader coverage that the URI handed to agents at the side-effects boundary is always the one the agent can resolve.

title: Copilot session restore splits one interaction into multiple chat responses
description:
## Type of Bug

Bug

## Description

Restoring an Agent Host Copilot session can split one SDK interaction into multiple AHP turns and therefore multiple `ChatResponseViewModel` instances. The additional requests have empty prompts.

The Copilot SDK can persist empty `assistant.message` events with no tool requests immediately before another assistant message in the same `interactionId` and SDK `turnId`. The live adapter ignores these non-renderable messages, but `mapSessionEvents` treats every parent assistant message without tool requests as the end of the current turn. The following assistant message then has no active builder, so history replay creates a fallback turn with an empty user message.

The resulting chain is:

1. `mapSessionEvents` prematurely finalizes the parent turn.
2. The next assistant message creates a fallback turn with an empty prompt.
3. `turnsToHistory` emits a request/response pair for every reconstructed turn.
4. `ChatServiceImpl` and `ChatViewModel` create multiple top-level response view models.

Captured restored models showed six empty requests created within the same millisecond. Their request IDs exactly matched the orphaned SDK `assistant.message` event IDs.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run a tool-heavy Copilot Agent Host conversation that produces multiple SDK model rounds.
2. Switch away from the session or restart/reopen it so history is rebuilt from SDK events.
3. Inspect the chat model or rendered transcript.
4. Observe multiple requests/responses with empty prompts for what was one live interaction.

## Expected Behavior

All assistant messages belonging to the same SDK interaction are reconstructed into one AHP turn and one top-level chat response, preserving markdown/tool ordering. Empty, non-renderable assistant events must not create a turn boundary.

## Relevant Code

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/mapSessionEvents.ts`
- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/mapSessionEvents.test.ts`

(Written by Copilot)

Browser `read_page` tool hangs the turn ("Evaluating") when called without required `pageId`
description:
## Summary

A `read_page` (Read Page) browser tool call gets stuck forever in **"Evaluating"** when the model invokes it with empty arguments (omitting the required `pageId`). The tool crashes synchronously inside `prepareToolInvocation`, which leaves the agent-host permission request unresolved and hangs the entire turn.

## Root cause

`createBrowserPageLink` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/tools/browserToolHelpers.ts` calls `pageId.toString()` without guarding against `undefined`:

```ts
export function createBrowserPageLink(pageId: string | URI): string {
	if (typeof pageId === 'string') { pageId = BrowserViewUri.forId(pageId); }
	return `[${BrowserEditorInput.DEFAULT_LABEL}](${pageId.toString()}?vscodeLinkType=browser)`; // throws when undefined
}
```

`ReadBrowserTool.prepareToolInvocation` calls `createBrowserPageLink(_context.parameters.pageId)`. When the model calls `readPage` with `{}`, `pageId` is `undefined` and `prepareToolInvocation` throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString')`.

Note that `ReadBrowserTool.invoke` already guards with `if (!params.pageId)` and returns a graceful error — but `prepareToolInvocation` runs first and crashes before `invoke` is ever reached.

This is not specific to `read_page`: nearly every browser tool (`navigate`, `click`, `type`, `hover`, `drag`, `handleDialog`, …) calls `createBrowserPageLink(params.pageId)` in `prepareToolInvocation`, so all share the same fragility.

## Evidence (from agent host logs)

1. `events.jsonl`: `tool.execution_start … toolName: 'readPage', arguments: {}` — required `pageId` omitted.
2. `Window.log`:
   - `[AgentHost] Invoking client tool: readPage (callId=toolu_01FgX…)`
   - `[LanguageModelToolsService#invokeTool] Error from tool read_page with parameters {}: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString'): TypeError` (stack: `createBrowserPageLink` → `prepareToolInvocation`)
   - `[AgentHost] Client tool rejected pre-execution: readPage Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString')`
3. `Agent Host.log`: `permission.requested … readPage` (custom-tool) is emitted, but unlike the sibling `bash` permission request — which receives `Permission response: approved=true` followed by `permission.completed` — the `readPage` request has **no `permission.completed`** and **no `tool.execution_complete`**. With the permission never resolved, the UI stays in "Evaluating" indefinitely.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a browser page in the integrated browser.
2. Have the agent call the `read_page` tool without a `pageId` argument (empty `{}`).
3. The Read Page tool call hangs in "Evaluating" and never completes.

## Fix

Make `createBrowserPageLink` resilient to a missing/empty `pageId` — return a plain label instead of throwing, so `prepareToolInvocation` succeeds and `invoke` returns its proper "No page ID provided" error to the model instead of hanging the turn.

## Related (separate, agent-host runtime — not this repo)

A pre-execution client-tool rejection should still emit `permission.completed` / `tool.execution_complete` so that a crashing client tool can never leave the turn stuck. Worth tracking separately in the Copilot CLI runtime.

title: Agents window: Changes view/modal shows no diffs when opening a session (possible race during session restore)
description:
Summary:
When opening a session in the Agents window the header shows there are changes, but the Changes view (right side) and the changes modal show no diffs. This appears intermittent and may be a race condition when a session is being restored.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Have VS Code open.
2. Open the session in the Agents window.
3. Search for a session that was open in VS Code and open it in Agents.
4. Observe the changes indicator in the header at the top showing there are changes.
5. The Changes view (right side) shows nothing.
6. Click the changes in the header to open the modal — the modal shows no changes.

Expected:
The Changes view and the changes modal should display the diffs corresponding to the header indicator.

Actual:
No changes are shown in the Changes view or modal despite the header indicating changes.

Additional details / context:
- This is intermittent and not reliably reproducible. I suspect a race condition when a session is being restored.
- This was discussed in Slack and is related to an earlier issue where changes are missing: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/320243
- There are logs attached to the related issue, but recent logs may help reproduce — previous logs were a bit stale.

Please investigate potential race conditions during session restore that could cause the Agents window to fail to populate the changes view/modal.


[View original Slack conversation](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C09MVCZKLP4/p1782496034381059?thread_ts=1782496034.381059&cid=C09MVCZKLP4)

title: Chat: Require double tildes for strikethrough rendering
description:
## Problem

Chat markdown rendering currently treats both `~text~` and `~~text~~` as strikethrough because Marked's GFM tokenizer accepts one or two tilde delimiters. This can accidentally strike out text when an agent uses unrelated single tildes.

The Markdown preview uses the stricter double-tilde syntax, so the two VS Code markdown surfaces behave inconsistently.

## Expected behavior

- `~text~` renders literally.
- `~~text~~` renders as strikethrough.
- Other GFM rendering remains unchanged.

(Written by Copilot)

title: `/compact` is not available in the AHP+CLI harness
Agent Host client tool hangs after active client removal; browser click invoked with empty args
description:
## Summary

A browser `clickElement` tool call can get stuck in `Preparing` after the Agent Host removes the active client. The click never reaches Playwright; the workbench invokes the browser tool with `{}` parameters and crashes during tool preparation.

## Observed

In an Agents/Copilot CLI session using built-in browser tools:

1. `openBrowserPage` succeeds.
2. `clickElement` on the initial `Start` button succeeds.
3. `screenshotPage` succeeds.
4. The next `clickElement` on the board's `Run` button stays stuck at `Preparing`.

The session event stream ends with:

```text
tool.execution_start clickElement
permission.requested clickElement
# no permission.completed
# no tool.execution_complete
```

## Key log evidence

The model requested valid arguments:

```json
{
  "element": "Run button on Research Agent",
  "pageId": "<page-id>",
  "ref": "e200"
}
```

But the workbench invoked the underlying browser tool with empty parameters:

```text
[AgentHost] Invoking client tool: clickElement
[LanguageModelToolsService#invokeTool] Invoking tool click_element with parameters {}
[error] Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString')
    at createBrowserPageLink(...)
    at ClickBrowserTool.prepareToolInvocation(...)
```

The AHP sequence for the same tool call was:

```text
chat/toolCallStart clickElement
chat/toolCallReady confirmed="not-needed"           # no toolInput
chat/toolCallComplete success=false error="Client <client-id> disconnected before completing clickElement"
chat/toolCallReady confirmation UI with real toolInput
```

About 6 seconds earlier, the same session received:

```text
session/activeClientRemoved clientId=<client-id>
```

## Suspected cause

This looks like an Agent Host/client-tool lifecycle race:

- The active client is removed from session state while the UI/client connection is still participating in the turn.
- A later client-contributed browser tool call is treated as orphaned/disconnected.
- The synthetic `toolCallReady` without `toolInput` is consumed by the workbench client-tool handler.
- The handler falls back to `{}` and invokes `click_element` before the later `toolCallReady` containing the real `toolInput` arrives.
- `ClickBrowserTool.prepareToolInvocation` assumes `pageId` is present, calls `createBrowserPageLink(undefined)`, throws, and the original Copilot tool execution remains stuck waiting for completion/permission state.

Relevant code paths:

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/protocolServerHandler.ts`
  - disconnected client tool call handling emits synthetic ready/complete events
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostSessionHandler.ts`
  - missing `toolInput` falls back to `{}` once status is not `Streaming`
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/tools/clickBrowserTool.ts`
  - `prepareToolInvocation` assumes `pageId` is defined

## Expected

A disconnected/orphaned client-tool call should fail cleanly and unblock the model/UI, or be retried with a replacement active client. It should not invoke the local browser tool with `{}` parameters or leave the tool call stuck in `Preparing`.

## Possible fixes

- Do not invoke client tools from `toolCallReady` events that lack `toolInput` when the tool has required arguments or `_meta.toolArguments` exists.
- Ensure disconnected-client synthetic `toolCallReady`/`toolCallComplete` ordering cannot race with later confirmation UI events for the same tool call.
- Harden browser tool `prepareToolInvocation` against missing `pageId` so malformed protocol state becomes a clean tool error.
- Investigate why `session/activeClientRemoved` fired while the client was still successfully confirming/completing tool calls in the same session.

title: Chat: BYOK models can trigger GitHub API rate limit and cause BYOK model requests to fail
description:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

When using BYOK models and logged into GitHub, if making too many requests to the BYOK models too quickly (which can occur when there are multiple subagents running or running chats in multiple workspaces), it can somehow trigger GitHub API rate limit. Furthermore, it causes all chats to instantly fail showing the model ID as the error message.

This does not happen when not logged into GitHub.

This is annoying and unexpected because it causes interruptions to my ongoing chats unexpectedly and had to restart the chat (either after waiting for the API rate limit to clear or logging out of GitHub in the extension), and restarting the chat might cause the model to get lost of the current progress easily. This is especially true when running multiple subagents, since the main agent can only see the subagent reporting an agent error and not seeing its work at all.

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.52.2026060505
- VS Code Version: 1.124.0-insider (0035c783eccf8a2efbdb972dfe62becb51f11fc6)
- OS Version: macOS 26.4.1

title: Bug: reasoningEffort setting written to wrong vendor section in chatLanguageModels.json
description:
# Bug: reasoningEffort setting written to wrong vendor section in chatLanguageModels.json

## Bug Description

When setting `reasoningEffort` for a model in the Chat Language Models configuration, the setting is written to the wrong vendor section in `chatLanguageModels.json`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure multiple custom endpoint vendors in `chatLanguageModels.json` (e.g., DeepSeek, MiMo, MyCustom)
2. Each vendor has different models defined
3. Select a model (e.g., `gpt-5.5` under MyCustom vendor) and set its `reasoningEffort` to `"high"` via the VS Code UI
4. Check the `chatLanguageModels.json` file

## Expected Behavior

The `settings` object with `reasoningEffort` should be added under the **MyCustom** vendor section where the `gpt-5.5` model is defined:

```json
{
    "name": "MyCustom",
    "vendor": "customendpoint",
    "models": [
        {
            "id": "gpt-5.5",
            "name": "gpt-5.5",
            "url": "http://127.0.0.1:15721",
            "toolCalling": true,
            "vision": true,
            "streaming": true,
            "thinking": true,
            "reasoningEffortFormat": "responses",
            "supportsReasoningEffort": [
                "none",
                "minimal",
                "low",
                "medium",
                "high",
                "xhigh"
            ],
            "maxInputTokens": 1050000,
            "maxOutputTokens": 128000
        }
    ],
    "settings": {
        "gpt-5.5": {
            "reasoningEffort": "high"
        }
    }
}
```

## Actual Behavior

The `settings` object is incorrectly written under the **DeepSeek** vendor section, which doesn't even contain a `gpt-5.5` model:

```json
{
    "name": "DeepSeek",
    "vendor": "customendpoint",
    "models": [
        {
            "id": "deepseek-v4-pro",
            "name": "deepseek-v4-pro",
            "url": "https://api.deepseek.com/v1",
            "toolCalling": true,
            "vision": true,
            "streaming": true,
            "thinking": true,
            "supportsReasoningEffort": [
                "high",
                "max"
            ],
            "maxInputTokens": 1000000,
            "maxOutputTokens": 384000
        }
    ],
    "settings": {
        "gpt-5.5": {
            "reasoningEffort": "high"
        }
    }
}
```

## Configuration File

File path: `%APPDATA%\Code\User\chatLanguageModels.json`

## Environment

- VS Code Version: 1.126.0
- OS: Windows
- Extension: GitHub Copilot Chat

## Suggested Labels

- `chat` or `copilot-chat`
- `bug`
- `settings`

title: Custom BYOK endpoint: "Sorry, no response was returned" when empty tool_calls: [] on content deltas
description: I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. Related closed issues: #255934, #253126 - Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in (0.53.1) - VS Code Version: 1.125.1 (x64) - OS Version: Windows 11 - Feature: Ask mode - Selected model: Custom BYOK endpoint — moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 via chatLanguageModels.json - Logs: ``` 2026-06-24 09:02:16.869 [info] ccreq:ed060600.copilotmd | badRequest | moonshotai/Kimi-K2.6 | 1126ms | [copilotLanguageModelWrapper] 2026-06-24 09:02:16.953 [info] [ToolCallingLoop] Stop hook result: shouldContinue=false, reasons=undefined ``` Steps to Reproduce: 1. Configure a custom endpoint in chatLanguageModels.json with toolCalling: true pointing to a vLLM-backed server (identified via system_fingerprint: "vllm-0.22.1" in responses) 2. Send any prompt in VS Code chat Expected: Response content is displayed. Actual: Model reasoning steps appear in the UI but no response content is shown — "Sorry, no response was returned." Root cause: vLLM emits "tool_calls": [] (empty array) on every content delta even when no tool call is being made. VS Code treats any tool_calls field presence as a tool invocation and discards the content, logging the request as badRequest. Confirmed by running a local proxy that strips empty tool_calls arrays — with the proxy in place requests log as success and respond correctly. Backends returning null instead of [] work fine. Example offending SSE chunk from the server: ``` {"choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"content":"Hello","tool_calls":[]},"finish_reason":null}]} ``` Previously reported in #255934 and #253126 (both closed). Suggested fix: Only process tool_calls deltas when the array is non-empty (tool_calls.length > 0).

title: Nudge EDU/Student users to Copilot Pro instead of Pro+ when limits are reached
description:
## Problem

EDU/Student users currently appear to be routed through the same quota messaging as the `individual` plan. In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatErrorMessages.ts`, `ChatEntitlement.EDU` maps to `copilotPlan: 'individual'`, and the quota messaging for `individual` tells users to upgrade to **Copilot Pro+**.

For EDU/Student users, we should nudge them to **Copilot Pro** instead.

## Expected

When EDU/Student users hit Copilot limits, the upgrade messaging should direct them to **Copilot Pro**, not **Copilot Pro+**.

## Notes

Relevant code paths:
- `getCopilotPlanFromEntitlement(ChatEntitlement.EDU)` currently returns `'individual'`
- `getQuotaMessageForPlan('individual', ...)` uses messaging that says to upgrade to Copilot Pro+

Type: Bug When I step in a multi-target debugging scenario, the source code and call stack should remain focused on the debug session/thread that I am stepping in. I am noticing that sometimes that is true, and sometimes the focus swaps to another debug session/thread that is stopped. For context, I am maintaining a custom debug adapter that performs remote debugging, so stepping can often take longer than 800ms. The behavior that I expect seems to conflict with the behavior that was introduced in these issues/commits and their followups: - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/30d73ea6dfafaa65c6aef8194f988475f105336c - https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/125144#issuecomment-869641057 In order to keep both of these behaviors, here are some ideas: - Create a user setting to choose whether focus should be automatically passed to another thread or not when the current one starts running - Create a user setting to adjust the timeout for the automatic focus passing - Add a new DAP property for StoppedEvent or use the existing "preserveFocusHint" to change focus back to the stopped thread if the focus has been passed away Let me know if you want me to recreate this with the Mock Debug Adapter. title: Copilot Chat auto-switches to 1M context after VS Code restart, ignoring selected model setting
description:
* Copilot Chat Extension Version: latest
* VS Code Version: latest
* OS Version: latest
* Feature: Copilot Chat / existing chat session after VS Code restart
* Selected model: GPT 5.5 High 272k

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set Copilot Chat to use GPT 5.5 High with 272k context.
2. Start or continue a Copilot Chat session.
3. Restart VS Code.
4. Continue the existing Copilot Chat session.
5. Check the model/context shown in the Copilot UI.

## Expected Behavior

Copilot should respect the currently selected model/context setting after VS Code restart.

If I selected GPT 5.5 High 272k, continuing an existing session should keep using GPT 5.5 High 272k, unless I explicitly choose another model/context.

## Actual Behavior

After restarting VS Code and continuing an existing session, Copilot appears to ignore the selected setting and silently switches to the 1M context option.

This is especially serious because 1M is much more expensive. The switch is not explicitly confirmed by the user, but the user is still charged for the more expensive option.

## Impact

This caused unexpected billing charges for me. In one case, I paid around $10 because Copilot silently switched to the 1M option.

This makes Copilot unsafe to use with paid models/context tiers, because the UI setting is not reliably respected across VS Code restarts.

## Request

Please investigate why continuing an existing session after VS Code restart can override the user-selected model/context setting.

At minimum, Copilot should never silently switch to a more expensive model/context tier without explicit user confirmation.

title: Start Menu pinned tile becomes invisible (transparent) after every auto-update on   Windows
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->

<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
  Environment:
  - OS: Windows 10 22H2 (19045)
  - VS Code version: 1.125.1 (happens every update, across multiple versions)
  - Install type: System Installer, custom path E:\Program Files\ide\Microsoft VS Code

  Steps to reproduce:
  1. Pin VS Code to the Start menu (tile area). The tile displays correctly.
  2. Wait for an auto-update, or trigger one via "Check for Updates".
  3. After the update completes, open the Start menu.

  Observed behavior:
  The pinned VS Code tile becomes completely invisible/transparent (not a white square —
  truly empty, nothing renders). The shortcut itself is intact, Code.exe exists at the
  correct path, and clicking the invisible tile still launches VS Code normally.

  Workaround that works every time:
  Right-click the blank tile → "Unpin from Start" → re-pin from Code.exe. Or, right-click
  the .lnk shortcut → Properties → Shortcut tab → "Change Icon..." → OK → Apply (without
  actually changing the icon). Both restore the tile immediately.

  What has been ruled out:
  - ❌ Shortcut target path is NOT broken — TargetPath still points to correct Code.exe
  and IconLocation is Code.exe,0
  - ❌ No _ (underscore) subfolder issue — Code.exe is directly in install directory, not
  moved
  - ❌ Icon cache corruption — ie4uinit.exe -show alone doesn't always fix it; restarting
  StartMenuExperienceHost.exe does
  - ❌ Not specific to custom install path — the Code.VisualElementsManifest.xml and its
  referenced hash-named PNG folder are both intact post-update



  Possible root cause (AI-generated analysis):
  The root cause appears to be that VS Code's Inno Setup-based updater replaces Code.exe
  in-place during the update but does not call SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, ...) or
  ie4uinit.exe -ClearIconCache after the file replacement. Windows' Start menu tile host
  process (StartMenuExperienceHost.exe) holds a cached rendering of the old Code.exe's
  icon resources in memory. Because the file path hasn't changed, Windows does not
  automatically invalidate the cache, and the stale cached data fails to map to the new
  binary's icon resources — resulting in the tile rendering nothing (invisible rather than
  a white fallback).

  Additionally, Code.VisualElementsManifest.xml references icon PNGs via a hash-named
  subfolder (e.g. <hash>\resources\app\resources\win32\code_150x150.png). Even though the
  manifest is updated to the new hash during installation, if StartMenuExperienceHost.exe
  has cached the manifest content from before the update, it may still reference the old
  (now-deleted) hash folder path. This would also cause a transparent tile.

  Suggested fix:
  In the Inno Setup installer script, add a post-install step:

  [Code]
  procedure CurStepChanged(CurStep: TSetupStep);
  begin
    if CurStep = ssPostInstall then
      SHChangeNotify(SHCNE_ASSOCCHANGED, SHCNF_IDLIST, 0, 0);
  end;

  Or in the [Run] section:

  [Run]
  Filename: "{cmd}"; Parameters: "/c ie4uinit.exe -ClearIconCache"; Flags: runhidden

title: Bug: Custom endpoint crashes with "No lowest priority node found" under context limits and silently ignores plain-text apiKey
description:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: [Please fill from the Extensions tab, e.g., v0.23.0]
- VS Code Version: [Please fill from VS Code -> About, e.g., 1.90.1]
- OS Version: macOS (MacBook Air)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Custom Language Model Integration (chatLanguageModels.json)
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Custom Endpoint (minimaxai/minimax-m3 via NVIDIA NIM)
- Logs: See below

### Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure a custom endpoint in `chatLanguageModels.json` with `"toolCalling": true` and `"maxInputTokens": 16000` (or 8000 to match typical trial API constraints).
2. Install any agent extensions that register multiple tools/schemas (e.g., extensions that register dozens of custom tools, bloating the prompt payload).
3. Open Copilot Chat, select the custom model, and send a message.
4. The client-side token-pruning algorithm crashes with a fatal exception.

---

### Description and Root Cause

I am configuring a custom language model (`minimaxai/minimax-m3` on NVIDIA NIM) using the `chatLanguageModels.json` configuration in VS Code.

When using the model with `"toolCalling": true`, the extension crashes locally with the following error:
`Error: No lowest priority node found (path: Xre) at eEt (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:173:4513)`

**Detailed Root Cause:**
1. **Excessive Tool Injection:** VS Code automatically injects the JSON schemas of all available agent/extension tools (in my case, over 70 tools totaling ~86KB) into the payload.
2. **Pruning Algorithm Failure:** When trying to compress the prompt payload to fit a lower `"maxInputTokens"` constraint (such as 8000 or 16000) to respect the custom API limits, the token-pruning algorithm fails to safely discard low-priority nodes and throws a fatal client-side exception: `No lowest priority node found`.
3. **UI Selection Disappearance:** If I try to work around this by setting `"toolCalling": false` in `chatLanguageModels.json`, the custom model completely disappears from the Copilot Chat model selection dropdown UI, making it impossible to use without tool injection.

---

### Call Stack / Error Logs:

```text
Error: No lowest priority node found (path: Xre)
    at eEt (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:173:4513)
    at n.removeLowestPriorityChild (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:171:10945)
    at on._getFinalElementTree (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:174:30965)
    at async on.renderRaw (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:174:29509)
    at async on.render (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:174:29172)
    at async on.render (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1686:16979)
    at async FG._provideLanguageModelResponse (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1710:11644)
    at async FG.provideLanguageModelResponse (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1710:15097)
```

---

### Related Bug: Plain-text `apiKey` silently ignored in configuration

During troubleshooting, we also found that if an API key is provided as a plain string in `chatLanguageModels.json`:
`"apiKey": "nvapi-SK1VhLO..."`

VS Code does not raise a configuration error. Instead, it silently drops/ignores the key and sends the HTTP request to the custom endpoint with **no `Authorization` header at all**, leading to authorization failures on the receiving server. 

The header is only populated if we force VS Code to use the secret store reference syntax:
`"apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.nvidia-api-key}"`

---

### Expected Behavior
1. **Tool Control**: Setting `"toolCalling": false` in `chatLanguageModels.json` should successfully disable tool schema injection, but the model must remain selectable in the UI dropdown.
2. **Robust Pruning**: The token-pruning engine should degrade gracefully (e.g., truncation or dropping systemic messages) without raising fatal runtime exceptions when payload constraints are tight.
3. **Consistent Auth**: VS Code should support plain-text API keys in `chatLanguageModels.json` as fallback, or at least throw a validation warning/error instead of silently omitting the Authorization header in the outgoing HTTP requests.

title: Chat model picker crashes with 'a.charAt is not a function'
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->

## Summary

Clicking the model picker button in VS Code Chat throws `TypeError: a.charAt is not a function` and the dropdown never appears. The crash happens in `getCategoryLabel()` in `chatModelPicker.ts` when it receives a non-string `category` value (including `null` or omitted). The function only guards against `undefined` and `''` in the switch, then unconditionally calls `.charAt(0)` in the default branch.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: **No**

This is important: the crash is in VS Code's code, not an extension. With all extensions disabled, only Copilot's built-in models register, and those always provide string categories like `'lightweight'`, so the bug doesn't manifest. But the picker still crashes on any third-party provider that omits `category` or passes `null`, which is valid per the API spec (`category?: string`).

I filed this here (not on the extension publisher) because the root defect is the unguarded `.charAt` call in VS Code's picker code. The extension already shipped a workaround in v2.1.6, but the upstream bug means the next extension that doesn't guard `category` will hit the exact same crash.

## Version

- VS Code Version: **Insiders 1.126** (bug introduced here; **Stable 1.125 not affected** — same provider, same account, same quota state, picker works fine there)
- OS Version: **macOS 26.5**
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: built-in (bundled with VS Code)
- Feature: model picker (clicking the model picker button in the Chat input)
- Selected model: N/A — crash happens before any model is selected

## Extensions

The bug requires a BYOK provider registered via `vscode.lm.registerLanguageModelChatProvider` to trigger. I have one extension installed: `gethnet.litellm-connector-copilot` (LiteLLM-backed OpenAI-compatible proxy, vendor: `litellm-connector`). With that extension disabled (or all extensions disabled), the picker opens normally because the only models registered are Copilot's own, which all carry a known string `category`.

Extension Bisect was not used because the crash is in VS Code's code, not the extension's. The extension simply provides a `LanguageModelChatInformation` entry whose `category` field was set to a grouping object `{ label: <string>, order: <number> }` — a non-string value. VS Code's picker iterates all registered models, hits `getCategoryLabel` with that value, and throws.

## Steps to Reproduce

The bug appears when:
1. A language model provider (built-in or third-party) registers a model via `vscode.lm.registerLanguageModelChatProvider` where `LanguageModelChatInformation.category` is not a string (e.g., omitted, `null`, or an object).
2. You click the model picker button in the Chat input (or invoke `workbench.action.chat.openModelPicker`).

**Why quota exhaustion in the original report:** I discovered this with Copilot's quota exhausted because that's when the picker starts showing "Other Models" (third-party vendors). On an active Copilot subscription, the only models listed are Copilot's own, which all use valid string categories, so the bad code path never runs. The bug exists regardless of quota state—it's just more visible (and discoverable) once Copilot models are unavailable.

## Expected Behavior

The picker dropdown should appear and list all registered models. If `category` is non-string, missing, `null`, or empty, the picker should treat it the same way it already handles `undefined` and `''` — omit the category tag and move on.

## Actual Behavior

The dropdown does not appear. No error toast, no log channel entry. The console records one `TypeError: a.charAt is not a function` per click, one per registered model.

## Console Output

Three identical traces on three consecutive clicks:

```
chatModelPicker.ts:331 Uncaught TypeError: a.charAt is not a function
    at TSn (chatModelPicker.ts:331:1)
    at L0i (chatModelPicker.ts:1547:1)
    at fbe (chatModelPicker.ts:223:1)
    at RSn (chatModelPicker.ts:612:1)
    at IWe.show (chatModelPicker.ts:1146:1)
    at chatModelPicker.ts:1065:1
    at HTMLAnchorElement.<anonymous> (chatModelPicker.ts:1085:1)
getCategoryLabel     @ chatModelPicker.ts:331
getModelHoverContent @ chatModelPicker.ts:1547
createModelItem      @ chatModelPicker.ts:223
buildModelPickerItems @ chatModelPicker.ts:612
show                 @ chatModelPicker.ts:1146
(anonymous)          @ chatModelPicker.ts:1065
(anonymous)          @ chatModelPicker.ts:1085
```

Quota state in the same session:

```
log.ts:117 ERR You've reached your monthly credit limit. Upgrade to Copilot Pro or wait until your credits reset on June 30, 2026 at 7:00 PM.
    ChatQuotaExceeded: You've reached your monthly credit limit.
        at OG._provideLanguageModelResponse (.../copilot/dist/extension.js:1690:14186)
```

## Root Cause

In `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatModelPicker.ts`, the function `getCategoryLabel` has a type signature that says `category: string | undefined`, but the code doesn't match:

```ts
function getCategoryLabel(category: string | undefined): string | undefined {
    switch (category) {
        case undefined:
        case '':
            return undefined;
        case 'lightweight': return localize(...);
        case 'versatile':   return localize(...);
        case 'powerful':    return localize(...);
        default:
            return category.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + category.slice(1);  // ← crashes here
    }
}
```

The problem: JavaScript `switch` uses **strict equality**, so `case undefined` only matches `undefined`, not `null`. If `category` is `null`, an object, a number, or any other non-string value, it falls through to `default:` where `.charAt(0)` is called unconditionally. That throws.

The public API for `LanguageModelChatInformation` declares `category?: string`, meaning providers are allowed to omit it entirely or pass `null`. VS Code should handle that gracefully, but instead one bad model aborts the entire picker dropdown.

The same `.charAt` pattern appears in two other functions in the same file:
- `getPriceCategoryLabel`
- `getVendorDisplayName`

Both have the same unguarded fallback that will throw on non-string input.

## Suggested Fix

Add a `typeof` guard before the switch, treating non-strings the same way undefined and empty string are already handled:

```ts
function getCategoryLabel(category: string | undefined): string | undefined {
    if (typeof category !== 'string' || category.length === 0) {
        return undefined;
    }
    switch (category) {
        case 'lightweight': return localize('chat.category.lightweight', "Lightweight");
        case 'versatile':   return localize('chat.category.versatile',   "Versatile");
        case 'powerful':    return localize('chat.category.powerful',    "Powerful");
        default:
            return category.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + category.slice(1);
    }
}
```

Apply the same guard to `getPriceCategoryLabel` and `getVendorDisplayName` in the same file. This is behavior-preserving: existing translations stay the same, and any non-string category just gets omitted from the UI instead of crashing.

Optionally (for better diagnostics): add a `logService.warn` in the guard so silent picker crashes show up in the Log (Window) output instead of being invisible outside DevTools.

## Additional Context

**Silent failure.** The crash is invisible in the UI — no error toast, no log channel entry, no status bar hint. Only DevTools console shows the exception. This makes it hard for users to diagnose why the picker won't open.

**Why it's rare today.** Most users see Copilot models first, which all use correct string categories, so the bug path doesn't run. But the picker should be defensive against *any* model with a missing or malformed `category`, not just happen to work because Copilot's descriptors are well-formed.

**Why this is VS Code's responsibility, not the extension's.** The API spec for `LanguageModelChatInformation` declares `category?: string` — it's optional, and it's optional for a reason (not every provider needs or wants to categorize their models). Code that consumes optional fields should always guard against their absence. VS Code's picker iterates and renders models from multiple vendors; it's responsible for handling any value an extension can legally supply under the API contract. This isn't about a misconfigured extension—it's about defensive programming in code that has to work with many different providers.

**Our workaround.** The LiteLLM Connector extension (v2.1.6, already shipped) fixed its side by ensuring `category` is always a valid string. This issue exists to harden the picker itself so future extensions don't need the same workaround.

title: [Bug] Model Picker Configuration Not Persisted to `chatLanguageModels.json` — Third-Party Providers Cannot Receive User-Configured Model Settings
description:
## Summary

When a user adjusts model parameters (e.g. **Reasoning Effort**, **Context Size**, **Service Tier**) via the **Chat Model Picker dropdown**, the values are correctly persisted for the current chat editor, but third-party `LanguageModelChatProvider` extensions receive the previously persisted value from `chatLanguageModels.json` or the schema default — not the user-selected value — in `modelConfiguration` at request time. The user-visible settings do not flow into the API surface used by non-Copilot providers.

---

## Regression Window

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Last Known Good** | VS Code **1.124.2** (2026-06-10) |
| **First Known Bad** | VS Code **1.125.0** (2026-06-17) — also **1.125.1** |
| **Root Cause PR** | [#321011](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321011) — *Fix model configurations syncing across editors and locations* |
| **Underlying Issue** | [#320393](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/320393) — *Context length selector changes on all open editors* |
| **Milestone** | [1.125.0](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/milestone/424) |
| **Files Changed** | `+725 / −58` across ~8 files |

### What the PR Did

PR [#321011](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321011) introduced **per-editor scoped model configuration** to fix a bug where changing context size in one editor affected all other open editors. The key additions were:

- **`chatModelConfigurationStore.ts`** — Per-editor `IStorageService` bucket (resolves per `(location, sessionType)` key)
- **`chatModelConfigurationLogic.ts`** — Resolution logic: `resolveModelConfiguration()`, `computeStoredConfiguration()`, `filterConfigurationToSchema()`, `extractSchemaDefaults()`
- **`modelPickerActionItem.ts`** — `IModelConfigurationAccess` interface (read/write/actions contract)
- **Modifications to `chatInputPart.ts`** — Routes model picker reads/writes through `ChatModelConfigurationStore`
- **Modifications to `chatService.ts` / `chatServiceImpl.ts`** — Passes `userSelectedModelConfiguration` through to requests
- **Modifications to `languageModels.ts`** — Extracted `createModelConfigurationActions()` helper

### What Broke

Before 1.125.0, model picker wrote configuration **directly** via `LanguageModelsService.setModelConfiguration()` → both the global `_modelConfigurations` Map and `chatLanguageModels.json`. After the change, the primary write targets the per-editor `IStorageService` bucket, and only *mirrors* to the global service as a secondary operation. The mirror write (`ChatModelConfigurationStore.setModelConfiguration()` → `LanguageModelsService.setModelConfiguration()`) has a **hidden dependency**: it requires the model's metadata to already exist in `_modelCache`. When `_modelCache` is not yet populated (e.g. provider registered asynchronously), `setModelConfiguration()` silently exits without writing anything.

| | **1.124.2 (Good)** | **1.125.0 (Bad)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Primary write** | `LanguageModelsService.setModelConfiguration()` | `ChatModelConfigurationStore._applyLocalModelConfiguration()` → per-editor bucket |
| **Global mirror** | N/A (it was the primary) | `LanguageModelsService.setModelConfiguration()` → ⚠️ depends on `_modelCache` hit |
| **Copilot reads** | `ChatRequest.modelConfiguration` ← ChatInputPart | `ChatRequest.modelConfiguration` ← `ChatModelConfigurationStore` ✅ |
| **3rd-party provider reads** | `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions.modelConfiguration` ← `_modelConfigurations` ✅ | Same path, but `_modelConfigurations` may be empty ⚠️ |

---

## Environment

- **VS Code Version**: ≥ 1.125.0 (Insiders / Stable)
- **OS**: All platforms
- **Affected APIs**: `vscode.lm.registerLanguageModelChatProvider` / `LanguageModelChatProvider`

---

## Root Cause Analysis

### The Silent Failure Path

| | **Channel ①: Per-Editor Bucket** | **Channel ②: Global `_modelConfigurations`** | **Channel ③: `chatLanguageModels.json`** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Storage** | `IStorageService` KV store | In-memory `Map<string, IStringDictionary>` | Filesystem JSON |
| **Written by** | `ChatModelConfigurationStore._applyLocalModelConfiguration()` | `LanguageModelsService.setModelConfiguration()` | `LanguageModelsConfigurationService` |
| **Write reliability** | ✅ Always succeeds | ⚠️ Depends on `_modelCache` hit | ⚠️ Depends on Channel ② |
| **Read by Copilot** | ✅ `userSelectedModelConfiguration` | ❌ Not used | ❌ Not used |
| **Read by 3rd-party LM providers** | ❌ Not accessible | ✅ `getModelConfiguration()` | ❌ Not read directly |

### The Silent Failure

The critical issue is in [`LanguageModelsService.setModelConfiguration()`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts):

```typescript
async setModelConfiguration(modelId: string, values: IStringDictionary<unknown>): Promise<void> {
    const metadata = this._modelCache.get(modelId);
    if (!metadata) {
        return;  // ⚠️ SILENT RETURN — no write, no error, no warning!
    }
    // ...
    // 1. Update _modelConfigurations (in-memory)
    // 2. Write to chatLanguageModels.json
    // 3. Fire onDidChangeLanguageModels event
}
```

When `_modelCache` does not contain the model metadata (e.g., because the extension provider registered asynchronously and the cache was not yet populated, or was cleared during model re-resolution), the method **silently exits** without:
- Updating `_modelConfigurations` (the cache from which third-party providers read)  
- Writing to `chatLanguageModels.json`  
- Throwing or logging any error  

### Why Copilot Is Unaffected

Copilot participates via the `ChatParticipant` API. Its request path receives configuration through `ChatRequest.modelConfiguration`, which is sourced from `ChatInputPart.getModelConfiguration()` → `ChatModelConfigurationStore.getModelConfiguration()` — the **per-editor bucket (Channel ①)**:

```typescript
// chatServiceImpl.ts
modelConfiguration: options?.userSelectedModelConfiguration
    ?? (options?.userSelectedModelId
        ? this.languageModelsService.getModelConfiguration(options.userSelectedModelId)
        : undefined),
```

The primary value comes from `userSelectedModelConfiguration` (Channel ①), which is always available. The fallback to `getModelConfiguration()` (Channel ②) is only used when that primary source is absent.

### Why Third-Party Providers Are Affected

Third-party `LanguageModelChatProvider` implementations receive configuration through `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions.modelConfiguration`, which is populated from `LanguageModelsService.getModelConfiguration()` — the **global `_modelConfigurations` cache (Channel ②)**:

```typescript
// languageModelsService.sendChatRequest()
async sendChatRequest(modelId, from, messages, options, token) {
    const configuration = this.getModelConfiguration(modelId);
    const mergedOptions = configuration
        ? { ...options, configuration: { ...configuration, ...options.configuration } }
        : options;
    return provider.sendChatRequest(modelId, messages, from, mergedOptions, token);
}
```

If Channel ② was never populated with the user's latest picker selection (due to the silent failure above), `modelConfiguration` arrives as the previously persisted value from `chatLanguageModels.json` or the schema default.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install a third-party extension that registers a `LanguageModelChatProvider` with a `configurationSchema` (e.g. one providing `reasoningEffort` and `contextSize` properties).
2. Open the Chat view and select the third-party model from the model picker.
3. In the model picker dropdown, change **Reasoning Effort** or **Context Size** to a non-default value (e.g., `max`).
4. Send a chat request using this model.
5. Observe in the extension's handler that `options.modelConfiguration` contains the previously persisted value from `chatLanguageModels.json` or the schema default — never the value just selected in the picker.

### Expected

- Third-party providers should receive the user-selected configuration values from the model picker in `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions.modelConfiguration`.

### Actual

- `options.modelConfiguration` at request time contains the value from `chatLanguageModels.json` or the schema default, not the value the user just selected in the model picker.
- The model picker UI shows the correct selected value (because it reads from the per-editor bucket), but the actual request uses the persisted/default value visible to third-party providers.

---

## Proposed Fix

### Short-term

At minimum, `setModelConfiguration()` should **log a warning** when `_modelCache` is missing a model, so the silent failure is visible. Additionally, consider retrying the write when the model becomes available:

```typescript
async setModelConfiguration(modelId: string, values: IStringDictionary<unknown>): Promise<void> {
    const metadata = this._modelCache.get(modelId);
    if (!metadata) {
        this._logService.warn(`[LM] Cannot persist configuration for '${modelId}': model not yet resolved in cache`);
        // Optionally: queue the write for when the model resolves
        return;
    }
    // ...
}
```

### Long-term

1. **Unify the two configuration channels** so there is a single source of truth for per-model configuration, accessible equally to Copilot and third-party providers.
2. **Expose per-editor model configuration** to extensions through a stable API, so `LanguageModelChatProvider` implementations can access the user's current selection without relying on the global cache.
3. **Make `chatLanguageModels.json` or a unified service the canonical persistence layer** for all model configuration, ensuring that changes from the model picker are always written to the file/service and are consistently read by all consumers, including third-party providers.

---

## Related Files

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatModelConfigurationStore.ts` | Per-editor scoped storage (Channel ①) |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatModelConfigurationLogic.ts` | Resolution, filtering, schema extraction |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/languageModels.ts` | `setModelConfiguration()` / `getModelConfiguration()` / `sendChatRequest()` (Channel ②) |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/languageModelsConfigurationService.ts` | `chatLanguageModels.json` read/write (Channel ③) |
| `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostLanguageModels.ts` | Extension host: `$startChatRequest` — bridges `modelConfiguration` to provider |
| `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadLanguageModels.ts` | Main thread: registers provider & proxies `sendChatRequest` |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts` | Chat service: merges `userSelectedModelConfiguration` → `modelConfiguration` |

---

## Impact

This bug affects **all third-party `LanguageModelChatProvider` extensions** that declare a `configurationSchema` and rely on `ProvideLanguageModelChatResponseOptions.modelConfiguration` to receive user-configured model parameters (reasoning effort, context size, service tier, etc.).

title: AHP: Sub-agent results lost when parent agent ends turn before sub-agent completes
description:
## Problem

When a session invokes a skill that spawns a sub-agent (e.g. `review-areas` spawning a rubber-duck sub-agent), the main agent can end its turn/session *before* the sub-agent finishes. The sub-agent's results are delivered to its child channel but never relayed back to the main channel — the user only sees the "waiting for results" message.

## Observed behavior

1. Main agent (opus-4.6) invokes review skill → sub-agent (gpt-5.5) spawned on child channel
2. Main model emits `end_turn` after just "Kicked off the deep multi-angle review — waiting for results." (17 output tokens)
3. `sessionEnd` fires for main agent
4. Sub-agent works for ~90s, produces 8294 chars of review findings on child channel
5. `chat/turnComplete` fires for the main turn
6. User sees session idle with only the "waiting" message — review results are orphaned

## Expected behavior

Sub-agent results should be surfaced to the user on the main channel, either by:
- Keeping the parent session alive until sub-agents complete, or
- Relaying sub-agent `responsePart` content to the parent channel upon sub-agent completion

## Logs

Session `a867cc0d`, turn `request_fdfc4def`, 2026-06-20T18:32:52Z. Agent Host log shows:
```
Turn ended: 2
Hook started: sessionEnd
Hook ended: sessionEnd
...5s gap...
[sub-agent starts working on child channel]
...90s later...
Subagent completed: rubber-duck
chat/turnComplete
Session idle
```

title: Copilot Chat BYOK `vendor: openai` appears to ignore `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens`
description:
VS Code Version:
1.125.1

Copilot Chat Version:
0.53.1

OS:
Windows 11

Description:
When configuring an OpenAI BYOK model through `chatLanguageModels.json` with `vendor: openai`, Copilot Chat appears to ignore the configured `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens` values.

The same configuration, when changed from `vendor: openai` to `vendor: customendpoint`, appears to honour the configured token limits correctly.

The documentation appears to imply that these model-level settings are valid for providers including `openai`, because the model configuration reference lists `vendor` examples including `azure`, `openai`, and `customendpoint`, and then lists `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens` as model-level properties. The docs also say VS Code uses the sum of these two values as the model's total context window in the Chat view.

If these settings are not intended to be supported for `vendor: openai`, the documentation should say that clearly. If they are intended to be supported, this appears to be a bug.

Model configuration:
The model is configured through `chatLanguageModels.json`, not selected from the standard built-in Copilot model list.

The relevant OpenAI provider entry uses the Responses API:

    vendor: openai
    apiType: responses
    model id: gpt-5.5
    streaming: true
    toolCalling: true
    vision: true
    thinking: true
    zeroDataRetentionEnabled: true
    reasoningEffort: medium
    maxInputTokens: 272000
    maxOutputTokens: 128000
    url: https://api.openai.com/v1/responses

Representative redacted configuration:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "OpenAI",
    "vendor": "openai",
    "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.REDACTED}",
    "models": [
      {
        "id": "gpt-5.5",
        "name": "GPT-5.5",
        "url": "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses",
        "apiType": "responses",
        "toolCalling": true,
        "vision": true,
        "thinking": true,
        "streaming": true,
        "maxInputTokens": 272000,
        "maxOutputTokens": 128000,
        "zeroDataRetentionEnabled": true,
        "supportsReasoningEffort": ["none", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"],
        "reasoningEffortFormat": "responses"
      }
    ],
    "settings": {
      "gpt-5.5": {
        "reasoningEffort": "medium"
      }
    }
  }
]
```

Expected:
The Context Window popover and context packing should use the configured model limits:

    maxInputTokens + maxOutputTokens
    272000 + 128000 = 400000 tokens

So the Chat UI should show a context window of approximately 400K tokens.

The configured `maxInputTokens` value should also be respected by context packing so that VS Code does not pack more input context than the configured cap.

Actual:
With `vendor: openai`, the Context Window popover showed a much larger context window, approximately:

    18.8K / 888K tokens

This suggests VS Code is using built-in or discovered metadata for the recognised OpenAI model instead of the manually configured `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens`.

Workaround / comparison:
Changing the same endpoint and model configuration to `vendor: customendpoint` causes the configured values to be honoured.

For example:

```json
[
  {
    "name": "OpenAI Custom Endpoint",
    "vendor": "customendpoint",
    "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.REDACTED}",
    "apiType": "responses",
    "models": [
      {
        "id": "gpt-5.5",
        "name": "GPT-5.5 Custom",
        "url": "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses",
        "apiType": "responses",
        "toolCalling": true,
        "vision": true,
        "thinking": true,
        "streaming": true,
        "maxInputTokens": 272000,
        "maxOutputTokens": 128000,
        "zeroDataRetentionEnabled": true,
        "supportsReasoningEffort": ["none", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"],
        "reasoningEffortFormat": "responses"
      }
    ],
    "settings": {
      "gpt-5.5": {
        "reasoningEffort": "medium"
      }
    }
  }
]
```

With `vendor: customendpoint`, the Context Window popover showed:

    18.8K / 400K tokens

That matches the configured total:

    272000 + 128000 = 400000 tokens

Impact:
This prevents users from reliably controlling context packing for BYOK OpenAI models.

In this specific case, the configured model has a pricing threshold based on input-token count. If VS Code ignores the configured `maxInputTokens` value and instead packs according to the model's larger maximum context window, a conversation can unexpectedly cross into the higher pricing tier.

This is especially problematic because the UI appears to advertise the larger effective context window when `vendor: openai` is used, suggesting that the larger value may be used by the context packer rather than only displayed incorrectly.

Suggested resolution:
If `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens` are intended to be supported with `vendor: openai`, ensure the OpenAI provider honours the configured model-level values and uses them for both:

- the Chat Context Window display
- context packing / prompt construction

If these settings are intentionally ignored or overridden for recognised OpenAI models when `vendor: openai` is used, please document that clearly in the BYOK / `chatLanguageModels.json` model configuration documentation.

Additional notes:
Other model-level settings may also be affected when using `vendor: openai`, but this has not been verified. The demonstrated issue is specifically with `maxInputTokens` and `maxOutputTokens`.

The current workaround is to configure the same OpenAI Responses API endpoint using `vendor: customendpoint`, where the configured token limits appear to be honoured.

title: Copilot Chat frequently fails with "Response contained no choices" using OpenAI Responses API BYOK model
description:
VS Code Version:
1.125.1

Copilot Chat Version:
0.53.1

OS:
Windows 11

Description:
Copilot Chat/Agent mode repeatedly fails during normal conversations with:

```
Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.

Client Request Id: <REDACTED_CLIENT_REQUEST_ID>

Reason: Response contained no choices.: Error: Response contained no choices.
    at FG._provideLanguageModelResponse
    (.../resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1710:14094)
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
    at async FG.provideLanguageModelResponse
    (.../resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1710:15097)
```

This happens multiple times per conversation. There does not appear to be a 100% reliable way to reproduce the problem but it inevitably happens the longer the conversation goes.

Model configuration:
The failing model is configured through `chatLanguageModels.json`, not selected from the standard built-in Copilot model list.

The relevant configuration is an OpenAI provider entry using the Responses API:

```
vendor: openai
apiType: responses
model id: gpt-5.5
streaming: true
toolCalling: true
vision: true
thinking: true
zeroDataRetentionEnabled: true
reasoningEffort: medium
maxInputTokens: 272000
maxOutputTokens: 128000
url: https://api.openai.com/v1/responses
```

This configuration is used so model requests can use zero data retention mode.

Local log correlation:
In local VS Code logs, each visible `Response contained no choices` error lines up with a Copilot Chat request summary marked `unknown` for the same configured `gpt-5.5` model via `copilotLanguageModelWrapper`.

Redacted examples:

```
<timestamp> ccreq:<REDACTED>.copilotmd | unknown | gpt-5.5 | <duration>ms | [copilotLanguageModelWrapper]
<timestamp> [CHAT] extension request ERRORED in STREAM Response contained no choices.

<timestamp> ccreq:<REDACTED>.copilotmd | unknown | gpt-5.5 | <duration>ms | [copilotLanguageModelWrapper]
<timestamp> [CHAT] extension request ERRORED in STREAM Response contained no choices.

<timestamp> ccreq:<REDACTED>.copilotmd | unknown | gpt-5.5 | <duration>ms | [copilotLanguageModelWrapper]
<timestamp> [CHAT] extension request ERRORED in STREAM Response contained no choices.
```

This pattern was found repeatedly in the same VS Code log session. The unredacted request IDs are available locally, but are redacted here because they may be uniquely trackable.

Relevant source-code path:
In current `microsoft/vscode`, this appears to flow through:

```
extensions/copilot/src/extension/conversation/vscode-node/languageModelAccess.ts
extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompt/node/chatMLFetcher.ts
extensions/copilot/src/platform/chat/common/commonTypes.ts
```

`languageModelAccess.ts` uses `debugName: 'copilotLanguageModelWrapper'` for the language model wrapper request.

`chatMLFetcher.ts` returns `ChatFetchResponseType.Unknown` with `RESPONSE_CONTAINED_NO_CHOICES` when no successful completion is produced from the completion stream.

`commonTypes.ts` defines:

```
export const RESPONSE_CONTAINED_NO_CHOICES = 'Response contained no choices.';
```

Impact:
This is user-visible and interrupts normal chat/agent workflows repeatedly. It does not appear to be prompt-specific. The failure appears to happen when the OpenAI Responses API configured model stream produces no usable completion choice, after which Copilot Chat classifies the request as `unknown` and surfaces the generic `Response contained no choices` error.

Expected:
Copilot Chat should either produce a response or surface a more actionable provider/model/backend error. If this is a valid upstream “no output” or malformed Responses API stream condition, the extension should handle it gracefully and show enough information to identify whether the issue is model output, Responses API parsing, streaming, tool-calling, reasoning output, or zero data retention mode.

Possible related issues:
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318235
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/313215
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316360

title: No credits spent shown when a request is stopped in Auto mode
description:
No credits spent shown when a request is stopped.

When a chat request is halted by the user, the chat does not show which model it chose in Auto mode, nor how many credits it spent.

This is important, since I've seen models freeze or start thinking in a loop and i cannot see which model was the failing one, nor see how many credits it spent.


<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: v0.53.0
- VS Code Version: 1.125.0
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26100 (Windows 11)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Chat
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): any
- Logs:

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Write a chat request, question, whatever using Auto for model selection.
2. Let it work for a little
3. Press the stop button to halt thinking and text/code generation
4. Look in the chat footnote for model and credits info, they are not there.

title: Extension host is unresponsive.
description:

Date: 2026-06-15T22:24:03Z
Electron: 42.2.0

Chromium: 148.0.7778.97
Node.js: 24.15.0
V8: 14.8.178.14-electron.0
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.19044

---

When I launch VS Code, the DevTools console first shows:

```
INFO Extension host (LocalProcess pid: 9768) is unresponsive.
```

Then, after a delay ranging from about 10–20 seconds to several minutes, it finally shows:

```
INFO Extension host (LocalProcess pid: 9768) is responsive.
```

During this entire period, both the **Search** and **Git** features are completely unusable (they do not respond or show any results). Other editor functionality may also be affected, but these two are the most noticeable.

**Expected behavior:** The extension host should become responsive quickly after startup, and Search/Git should be available without significant delay.

**Actual behavior:** The extension host stays unresponsive for a highly variable length of time (from seconds to minutes), during which Search and Git are blocked.

title: "Reserved for response" ignores `maxOutputTokens` for extension-contributed models (hard-coded to 8192)
description:
# Problem

The Copilot context window widget shows **"Reserved for response"** as ~8192 tokens for all extension-contributed models, regardless of the `maxOutputTokens` value declared by the provider.

**Expected:** "Reserved for response" reflects the actual `maxOutputTokens` reported by the `LanguageModelChatProvider` (e.g., 32768, 65536, etc.).

**Actual:** Always ~8192 tokens, making the reservation bar a tiny sliver even for models configured with large output budgets.

## Root Cause

In the Copilot Chat extension's internal endpoint wrapper, `ExtensionContributedChatEndpoint` ignores the provider's declared `maxOutputTokens` and returns a hard-coded value:

**File:** `extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/vscode-node/extChatEndpoint.ts`

```typescript
get maxOutputTokens(): number {
  // The VS Code API doesn't expose max output tokens, use a reasonable default
  return 8192;
}
```

This value flows into `toolCallingLoop.ts` where it's used as the `outputBuffer` for usage reporting:

```typescript
stream.usage({
  completionTokens: fetchResult.usage.completion_tokens,
  promptTokens: fetchResult.usage.prompt_tokens,
  outputBuffer: endpoint.maxOutputTokens,  // ← always 8192 for extension models
  promptTokenDetails,
});
```

Which then renders in `chatContextUsageWidget.ts` as the "Reserved for response" bar.

## Why This Matters

- Extension providers **do** report `maxOutputTokens` on `LanguageModelChatInformation` — but Copilot's internal wrapper never reads it
- For models with large output budgets (32K–128K), the UI misleads users into thinking only ~8K is reserved
- This is particularly misleading for reasoning/thinking models where output can legitimately be very large
- The `maxOutputTokens` value **is** used correctly for the actual vLLM `max_tokens` parameter — only the **display** is wrong

## Context

We've already solved the related issues in our extension (vLLM-2-Copilot):
- ✅ Token usage reporting via `LanguageModelDataPart` with `'usage'` MIME type and snake_case keys (not blocked by `isApiUsage()`)
- ✅ `prompt_tokens` / `completion_tokens` / `total_tokens` displayed correctly in the context widget
- ✅ `provideTokenCount` works for prompt budgeting

The only remaining gap is the `outputBuffer` / "Reserved for response" display.

## Proposed Fix

Option A (preferred): Read `maxOutputTokens` from the model information when constructing `ExtensionContributedChatEndpoint`:

```typescript
get maxOutputTokens(): number {
  return this.modelInfo.maxOutputTokens ?? 8192;
}
```

Option B: Expose `maxOutputTokens` on the `LanguageModelChat` API surface so Copilot can access it without reaching into provider internals.

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.120+
- Extension API: `LanguageModelChatProvider` (proposed `chatProvider`, version 5)
- Extension: vLLM-2-Copilot (https://github.tik.uni-stuttgart.de/ac120805/vLLM-2-Copilot)

## Screenshot

![Context Window Widget](screenshot-placeholder.png)
*Shows "Reserved for response" as a tiny bar (~8192) despite `maxOutputTokens: 32768` being configured and correctly reported by the provider.*

---

**Related:** This is a distinct issue from [#314722](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/314722) (usage = 0 for extension providers), which has already been addressed. The token counts (prompt, completion, total) display correctly — only the output reservation bar is affected.

title: Feature request: Display cache_write_price in the Cost column of the Models management UI
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

The **Cost (Credits per 1M Tokens)** column in the Models management UI currently displays **Input**, **Cache** (read), and **Output** costs. However, the CAPI `token_prices` response also includes a `cache_write_price` field that is not surfaced anywhere in the UI.

**Example CAPI response fragment:**

```json
"token_prices": {
    "batch_size": 1000000,
    "default": {
        "cache_price": 50,
        "cache_write_price": 625,
        "context_max": 200000,
        "input_price": 500,
        "output_price": 2500
    },
    "long_context": {
        "cache_price": 50,
        "cache_write_price": 625,
        "context_max": 936000,
        "input_price": 500,
        "output_price": 2500
    }
}
```

**Requested feature:**

Add a **"Cache write"** entry alongside the existing cost items (In, Cache, Out) in the Cost column so that users can see the full per-model pricing breakdown directly in the UI.

- Show `cache_write_price` (and its long-context variant) from the CAPI response in the same format as the other cost fields (e.g. "Cache write: 625").
- Include it in hover tooltips (e.g. "Cache write: 625 credits per 1M tokens").
- When the value is missing or null, display a consistent fallback matching the behavior for other absent costs.
- Support both default and long-context pricing rows in the model picker hover table.

**Why this matters:**

Cache write cost can be significantly higher than cache read cost (e.g. 625 vs 50 credits). Without this information in the UI, users cannot fully evaluate model pricing and may underestimate actual usage costs. The data is already returned by the API — it just needs to be displayed.

**Screenshot of current Cost column (Cache write is missing):**

![Cost column screenshot](https://github.com/github-copilot/chat/attachments/c55f7259-cbab-4429-a275-cc863e7189c6)

Type: Bug ## Description When using Fcitx5 Hangul in VS Code running natively on Wayland, active Hangul preedit text is discarded when I click another position in the editor. The composed Korean text is displayed with an underline, indicating that it is still in the IME preedit state. If I press Space before clicking, the text is committed and does not disappear. However, if I click another editor position while the underline is still visible, the entire preedit text disappears instead of being committed. The issue does not occur when VS Code is launched through XWayland with: ```bash code --ozone-platform=x11 ``` The issue also does not occur in GNOME Text Editor under the same desktop session and with the same Fcitx5 Hangul input method. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Log in to a GNOME Wayland session. 2. Use Fcitx5 with the Hangul input method. 3. Start VS Code normally using its native Wayland backend. 4. Open any editable file. 5. Type a Korean word, for example: ```text 테스트 ``` 6. Do not press Space, Enter, or an arrow key. Keep the text in the underlined preedit state. 7. Click another position in the editor. ## Actual Behavior The underlined Hangul preedit text is discarded and disappears. ## Expected Behavior The active preedit text should be committed before the caret moves to the clicked position. title: Run in terminal tool returns 'Failed to retrieve command output' when output exceeds scrollback
description:
## Problem

When a command's output exceeds the terminal's scrollback buffer (`terminal.integrated.scrollback`, default 1000 lines), the `run_in_terminal` tool returns "Failed to retrieve command output" instead of returning whatever is available in the buffer.

## Expected behavior

The tool should return the full scrollback buffer contents (i.e. the last N lines that fit in scrollback) rather than failing entirely. Even partial output is more useful than an error message.

## Repro

1. Set `terminal.integrated.scrollback` to a low value (e.g. 100)
2. Have the agent run a command that produces more lines than the scrollback (e.g. `seq 1 5000`)
3. Tool result says "Failed to retrieve command output"

## Notes

This is separate from the large output truncation/file-write handling in #321640 — that PR handles the case where output is successfully retrieved but exceeds the inline size limit. This issue is about output never being retrieved at all.

title: MCP tool input validation rejects anyOf schemas - blocks Union-typed parameters
description:
**VS Code Version:** 1.124.2 (6928394f91b684055b873eecb8bc281365131f1c, x64, Windows)

## Problem

When an MCP server exposes a tool with a parameter typed as a union (e.g. `Union[str, dict]` in Python/Pydantic), the resulting JSON Schema uses `anyOf`:

```json
{
  "fields_json": {
    "anyOf": [
      {"type": "string"},
      {"type": "object"},
      {"type": "null"}
    ],
    "default": null
  }
}
```

VS Code's MCP client-side validation rejects **all** inputs to these parameters with:

```
ERROR: Your input to the tool was invalid (must be string, must be null, must match a schema in anyOf)
```

The tool call never reaches the MCP server. The same tool works correctly with Claude Desktop's MCP client.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an MCP server (Python + FastMCP) with a tool that has a `Union[str, dict]` parameter:
   ```python
   @mcp.tool()
   def update_item(
       item_id: str,
       fields_json: Optional[Union[str, dict]] = None,
   ) -> str:
       ...
   ```
2. Call the tool from VS Code's agent/chat with a dict value for `fields_json`
3. Observe the `anyOf` validation error — the call never reaches the server

## Expected Behavior

The MCP client should pass the input through to the server when it matches **any** branch of the `anyOf` schema (a dict matches `{"type": "object"}`).

## Actual Behavior

The client rejects the input at validation time, reporting it doesn't match any branch.

## Workaround

Change all union-typed parameters to `Any`, which generates `{}` (unconstrained) in JSON Schema. This sacrifices type documentation to bypass the validation bug.
