title: Extension host OOM crash: glob.ts compiles an arbitrarily long watcher pattern into a pathological regex (regExp.test blows the V8 heap)
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: VS Code 1.124.2 (commit 6928394f91b684055b873eecb8bc281365131f1c)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.1 (arm64)

Note: local username scrubbed to `userx` in all captured strings.

## Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No (end-to-end), but the crash is reproducible WITH extensions disabled

The end-to-end crash is *triggered* by a language extension (gopls / vscode-go) supplying a bad watch pattern, so disabling all extensions removes the trigger. **However, the defect itself is in VS Code core** (`vs/base/common/glob.ts`) and is reproducible with no extensions at all by feeding the attached `pattern` directly to the `glob` API (see Steps to Reproduce) — `glob.parse(pattern)` + a single `match(path)` OOMs the host. So this is **not** an "extension bug" to forward to a publisher: the core defect is that `glob.ts` compiles an arbitrary, untrusted, multi-kilobyte string into a regex and runs it on every file event with no length or complexity guard, so a single malformed pattern from *any* extension can OOM-kill the entire extension host.

- VS Code Version: 1.124.2 (6928394f91b684055b873eecb8bc281365131f1c)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.1, arm64
- Insiders: the faulting code path (`glob.ts` `parseRegExp` / `regExp.test`) is unchanged on `main`, so this is expected to reproduce on the latest Insiders as well.

## Summary

A file-watcher **glob pattern** that is not a real glob — in my case the multi-line error output of a failed `go list` (~6.5 KB, dozens of `missing go.sum entry ...` lines) — gets compiled by `glob.ts` into an **8,691-character regex** containing **459 `[/\\]` path-separator character classes**. On the very next file-system event, `extHostFileSystemEventService.$onFileEvent` runs `regExp.test(path)` against that regex, which exhibits catastrophic backtracking / unbounded memory growth and **OOM-crashes the extension host**.

Because this happens inside the extension host, it silently kills any in-flight extension work. In my case it repeatedly cancelled in-flight GitHub Copilot Chat requests (they surfaced as `"Canceled"`), which is how I found it — but the editor-level defect is independent of Copilot.

The root problem is **defense-in-depth**: `glob.ts` trusts the pattern string completely. A malformed pattern should fail safe (be rejected / produce a non-matching matcher), never OOM the host.

## Steps to Reproduce

I have preserved the exact captured `pattern` and compiled `regExp` as a minimal repro. The shortest faithful reproduction:

```ts
import { parse } from 'vs/base/common/glob';

// `pattern` = the ~6.5 KB non-glob string captured from the watcher
// (the literal multi-line output of a failed `go list`, full of
//  "missing go.sum entry for module ... to add: go get ..." lines)
const pattern = /* contents of the attached `pattern` file */;

const match = parse(pattern);              // compiles to an ~8.6 KB regex
match('/users/userx/go/src/app/some/package/file.go');
// → catastrophic backtracking → V8 heap OOM
```

How it arises organically (real-world trigger):

1. Open a Go workspace where `go list ./...` fails (e.g. missing `go.sum` entries for an imported module).
2. gopls / vscode-go surfaces that **failure string** and it ends up registered as a **file-watch glob pattern** (a 6.5 KB multi-line string — clearly not a glob).
3. `glob.ts` compiles it into the pathological regex above.
4. Save any `.go` file → `$onFileEvent` → `regExp.test(path)` → extension host OOM.

## Smoking gun (extension-host debugger)

Running `Developer: Show Running Extensions` with a profile attached and reproducing the crash, the debugger paused with the banner **"PAUSED BEFORE OUT OF MEMORY EXCEPTION"**. Faulting frame and call stack (top-down):

```
<anonymous>                         glob.ts                            ← regExp.test(path) → OOM
n                                   glob.ts
<anonymous>                         extHostFileSystemEventService.ts
E._deliver / _deliverQueue / fire   event.ts
Dw.$onFileEvent                     extHostFileSystemEventService.ts   ← a file-system event
i._doInvokeHandler / _invokeHandler / _receiveRequest / _receiveOneMessage   rpcProtocol.ts
```

At the breakpoint:

- `path` = the `.go` file being saved (a path under my workspace)
- `regExp` = an **8,691-character** regex
- `pattern` = the **6,562-character** source string it was compiled from
- the regex contains **459 `[/\]`** separator classes

(The attached sanitized repro reproduces the same shape at 6,512 / 8,628 bytes and 495 separator classes.)

The `pattern` begins (sanitized — real package names replaced):

```
'/users/userx/go/src/app/go list failed to return compiledgofiles for "main".build constraints exclude all go files in /users/userx/go/pkg/mod/example.test/x/sys@v0.0.0/windowsmissing go.sum entry for module providing package example.test/module/group/area/section/pkg00 (imported by app/src/component/area/section/pkg00); to add:go get app/src/component/area/section/pkg00 ... (32 such "missing go.sum entry" entries) ...
```

The compiled `regExp` begins (sanitized):

```
/^'[/\]users[/\]userx[/\]go[/\]src[/\]app[/\]go list failed to return compiledgofiles for "main"\.build constraints exclude all go files in [/\]users[/\]userx[/\]go[/\]pkg[/\]mod[/\]example\.test[/\]x[/\]sys@v0\.0\.0[/\]windowsmissing go\.sum entry for module providing package exa ...
```

## Expected behavior

`glob.ts` should fail safe against pathological / non-glob patterns and never be able to OOM-crash the extension host:

- Reject or truncate patterns above a sane length (a 6.5 KB watch glob is never legitimate).
- Cap regex complexity (e.g. number of separator classes / alternations) and fall back to a literal/non-matching matcher when exceeded.
- Optionally guard `regExp.test` with a complexity or step budget.

A malformed watch pattern from an extension should at worst log a warning and not match — it must not be able to take down the host.

## Actual behavior

`glob.ts` compiles the 6.5 KB string into an 8,691-char regex; the first `regExp.test(path)` on a file event causes catastrophic backtracking and OOMs the extension host, silently killing all in-flight extension work.

## Attachments

Two files reproduce it deterministically (paths **sanitized**; structure/size preserved):

- `pattern.txt` — the ~6.5 KB non-glob source string (failed `go list` output)
- `regExp.txt` — the ~8.6 KB compiled pathological regex

(Drag these two files into the GitHub issue before submitting. They are sanitized: the local username is `userx` and all internal package paths are generic placeholders — only the failed-`go list` **structure** remains.)

## Notes on the upstream trigger (separate issue, FYI only)

The *source* of the bad pattern is gopls / vscode-go registering a failed `go list` error string as a watch glob. That is a second, separate bug I may file against `golang/vscode-go`. **This** issue is specifically about VS Code core (`glob.ts`) not being robust against such a pattern — that hardening protects against any extension (Go, .NET, or otherwise) leaking an oversized string into a watch pattern.

title: Agent terminal gets stuck on interactive package manager prompts (needrestart, debconf, pipe buffering)
description:
## Summary

The agent terminal tool fails to handle two classes of interactive prompts, causing consistent eval failures on terminalbench2 tasks that copilot-cli passes.

## Problem 1: needrestart/debconf TUI prompts

When `apt-get install` triggers needrestart, a "Which services should be restarted?" TUI prompt appears. None of the `detectsHighConfidenceInputPattern()` or `detectsLikelyInputRequiredPattern()` patterns in `outputMonitor.ts` match this format. The `idleSilence` timer fires after 60s, the tool returns "moved to background", and the agent gives up.

**Example**: `nginx-request-logging` — agent ran `apt-get install -y nginx`, needrestart prompted, agent waited 5 minutes then sent an empty `send_to_terminal` and stopped. copilot-cli finished the same task in 33 seconds.

## Problem 2: Pipe buffering hides prompts

When the model pipes an interactive command through `tail`/`head`/`grep`, the pipe buffers all output until the upstream closes. Interactive prompts (like opam `[Y/n]`) never reach the terminal buffer, so the `OutputMonitor` cannot detect them.

**Example**: `compile-compcert` — agent ran `opam install coq -y 2>&1 | tail -20`. The opam depext `[Y/n]` prompt was buffered by `tail` and never visible to the output monitor. The `[Y/n]` pattern *would* match `detectsHighConfidenceInputPattern` if it reached the terminal — the bug is the pipe hiding it.

## Fix

1. Set `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive` in the copilot agent terminal env vars (in `toolTerminalCreator.ts`), alongside existing `GIT_PAGER`, `GIT_EDITOR`, etc. This prevents apt/dpkg from ever opening interactive prompts.

2. Add system prompt guidance telling the model to never pipe interactive commands through filters.

## Impact

Found via terminalbench2 eval analysis comparing vscode-copilot-cli vs copilot-cli. These two issues account for 2 of 12 consistent regressions (~13% score gap).

## Issue Subcategory 
Links distinguished only by color 

## User Experience 
Users with color deficiencies cannot distinguish inline links from surrounding body text. They may miss important navigation options entirely. 

## Repro Steps 
Open VS Code > Copilot chat > Permission Picker combo box > Bypass approvals > “chat.permissions.default" link > Observe the issue: Links distinguished only by color 

## Actual Result 
The link “chat.permissions.default” is visually distinguished only by color (blue text) and does not have any additional non-color visual indicator such as underline or styling.

## Expected Result 
Links should have a non-color visual indicator (e.g., underline, bold text, or icon) in addition to color so that they are distinguishable from surrounding text for all users.

## How to Fix 
Add text-decoration: underline to inline links, or provide another non-color visual cue (bold, border-bottom). Ensure the link color also meets 3:1 contrast against surrounding text.

title: Screen reader announces incorrect numeric position for list items in Permission Picker combobox:A11y_VisualStudioCode_Permissions levels in Copilot CLI_ScreenReader
description:
## GitHub Tags
#A11yTCS;#Visual Studio Code Client; #SH_Integrated browser features_Win32_JUNE2026;#DesktopApp;#FTP;#Win32;#A11ySev2;#A11yMAS;#WCAG1.3.1;  #ScreenReader; #NVDA;

## Issue Subcategory 
List items not in a list container 

## User Experience 
Screen reader users cannot identify content as a list or hear the total item count. List navigation shortcuts (e.g., “L” key in JAWS) will not work. 

## Repro Steps 
Turn on NVDA screen reader > Open VS Code > Copilot chat > Permission Picker combo box > Observe the issue: Screen reader announces incorrect numeric position for list items in Permission Picker combobox

## Actual Result 
In the Permission Picker combo box, there are a total of 4 list items. However, while navigating using a screen reader, focus does not move to the 4th list item. After the 3rd item, the focus visually moves but the screen reader announces incorrect positional information such as “5 of 5”, even though only 4 items are present.

## Expected Result 
Screen reader focus should move sequentially to all list items, including the 4th item, and announce the correct positional information

## How to Fix 
Wrap list items in ul (unordered), ol (ordered), or dl (description) with the correct child elements (li, dt/dd). Alternatively, use ARIA roles such as role="list" and role="listitem" to remediate non-list markup as needed.

Application Name: VS Code

Edition Windows 11 Enterprise

title: VS Code does not reload modified .ipynb files when stored on external drives and edited on another machine
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
When working with .ipynb files stored on an external SSD and switching between two PCs, VS Code does not reload the updated notebook when reopening it on the first machine. Instead, it restores the old in‑memory notebook state.

To reproduce:  
1. Open a .ipynb on PC1.  
2. Close the VS Studio sesion with the .ipynb open, but saved on the external SSD
2. Modify and save it on PC2 (same file on external SSD).  
3. Return to PC1 and reopen VS Code.

I expected that VS Code detects the file changed on disk and reloads the new version, but VS Code restores the previous notebook state from memory and ignores the updated file on disk.

However, files.autoReload works for .py files but not for .ipynb; disabling hotExit and restoreWindows avoids the issue, but it is only a workaround, I think

Request:  
Please add an option for .ipynb files to always reload from disk when they change, or disable notebook state restoration.

# Feature Request: Respect metered network connections on Linux (NetworkManager)

## Problem

VS Code performs automatic update checks and extension update downloads regardless of whether the active network connection is marked as metered. On Linux, NetworkManager exposes this information system-wide via `connection.metered`, which applications are expected to respect to reduce background network activity on limited connections (mobile hotspots, tethered phones, satellite links, expensive roaming).

VS Code does not detect or respect this setting. In my opinion, the Auto-Update should be disabled when on an metered network.

## Expected Behavior

When the active connection is metered, VS Code should:

- suspend automatic update downloads, **or**
- offer a setting to disable update activity on metered connections

The auto check for new updates should be still possible, because it should not use huge amount of data. 
This should apply to VS Code application updates, extension update checks, and extension auto-downloads.

## Linux Integration

NetworkManager exposes the metered status via:

```bash
nmcli connection show <connection-name> | grep connection.metered
```

Values: `yes`, `no`, `unknown`. GNOME, KDE, Manjaro, Ubuntu, and Fedora all surface this in their network settings UI.

## Suggested Implementation

Detect `connection.metered` on Linux and pause background update activity automatically. Alternatively, expose a user setting:

```json
"update.respectMeteredConnections": true
```

description:

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: 1.123.0 and 1.124.0 (1.122.1 does NOT reproduce the issue)
- OS Version: CachyOS (Arch Linux based), kernel 7.0.12-1-cachyos, tested on both Wayland and X11 (--ozone-platform=x11)

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open VS Code (does not matter if a project is opened)
2. Trigger any action that opens a native confirmation dialog via DialogService#prompt, e.g.:
   - Help > About
   - Source Control > Sync (with git.confirmSync enabled)
   - Source Control > Discard Changes on a modified file
3. The entire window immediately becomes unresponsive (after a while turns grey/blank) as soon as the dialog is requested, and never recovers. VS Code must be force-killed.

What I expected: the dialog opens normally and the window remains responsive.

What actually happens: the whole window freezes the instant the dialog is requested.

Additional notes:
- Reproduced with extensions fully disabled (--disable-extensions), confirming this is not extension-related.
- Reproduced on both Wayland and XWayland (--ozone-platform=x11), so it does not appear to be Wayland-specific.
- Bisected via local package cache: 1.122.1-1.1 works correctly. 1.123.0-1.1 and 1.124.0-1.1 both reproduce the freeze.
- Git extension log (Git.log) shows the operation reaching the dialog and then nothing further:
  `DialogService#prompt This action will pull and push commits from and to "origin/<branch>"`
  immediately followed by repeated native crashpad errors:
  `[ERROR:third_party/crashpad/crashpad/snapshot/elf/elf_dynamic_array_reader.h:64] tag not found`
  `[ERROR:third_party/crashpad/crashpad/util/process/process_memory_range.cc:75] read out of range`
- Attempting to attach gdb/strace to the frozen main process (code/code.mjs) causes it to crash with SIGSEGV immediately on PTRACE_ATTACH/PTRACE_SEIZE, preventing further inspection this way.
- No additional errors appear in Dev Tools Console (Help > Toggle Developer Tools) before the freeze; the last console output is the DialogService#prompt trace line above.

Workaround: downgrading to 1.122.1 resolves the issue completely.

title: Agents Window: `New Chat` command fails when active session workspace uses unsupported scheme
description:
## Bug

When the active session in the Agents Window has a workspace with an unsupported URI scheme (e.g. `unknown:/`), the **New Chat** command (`workbench.action.sessions.newChat`) throws:

> No sessions provider can resolve folder 'unknown:/'

This surfaces as an error dialog and leaves the stale session active — the new-session composer never appears.

## Repro (via smoke tests)

1. Open the Agents Window
2. Start a Claude session (warmup) — the session's workspace resolves to `unknown:/`
3. After the warmup response, run `workbench.action.sessions.newChat`
4. **Expected**: new-session homepage (`.new-chat-widget-container`) appears
5. **Actual**: error dialog, session stays active, homepage never appears

This causes flaky failures in the `Test Claude session` and `Test Local session` smoke tests in the Agents Window suite. The "Chat Sessions" suite (normal workbench) is unaffected.

## Root Cause

`NewChatInSessionsWindowAction.run()` passes `sessionsManagementService.activeSession.get()?.workspace.get()?.uri` to `openNewSession({ folderUri })`. When that URI uses a scheme no provider supports, `_resolveProviderForNewSession` throws, and the error propagates unhandled.

## Fix

`SessionsViewService.openNewSession()` should catch the error from `createNewSession` and fall through to the folder-less composer view (the new-session placeholder), rather than propagating the error.

## CI Evidence

- **Failed run**: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/27446212747/job/81131834894?pr=321226#step:26:181
- **Failing tests**: `Test Claude session`, `Test Local session` (Agents Window suite, macOS / Electron)
- **Error**: `Timeout: get element '.sessions-chat-widget .new-chat-widget-container' after 60 seconds`
- Screenshot shows the error dialog with the `unknown:/` message

title: Agent Host sessions not restored on restart when chat.restoreLastPanelSession is true: possible AH lazy registration race (awaiting activation but missing new AH path) , bodyVersion":""
description:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Unknown

- VS Code Version: 
- OS Version: 

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Set "chat.restoreLastPanelSession": true in your settings.
2. Open one or more Agent Host (AH) chat sessions (e.g., Copilot Chat agent hosts).
3. Restart VS Code.
4. Observe that the Agent Host sessions are not restored after restart.

Notes:
- I suspect this is a race where the Agent Host is lazily registered. We may await extension activation but not the new AH path, so session restoration misses the AH instances that register later.

title: Terminal: glyphs overlap / are too close with Iosevka on Linux (WebGL renderer)
description: ## VS Code Version 1.123.0 (commit 6a44c352bd24569c417e530095901b649960f9f8, 2026-06-03) Electron: 42.2.0 / Chromium: 148.0.7778.97 / Node.js: 24.15.0 Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes ## OS Version Fedora 44, Linux kernel 7.0.8-200.fc44.x86_64 ## GPU / Driver NVIDIA RTX 3070, proprietary driver ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Install [Iosevka Term](https://github.com/be5invis/Iosevka/releases) or [Iosevka Fixed](https://github.com/be5invis/Iosevka/releases) v34.6.1 on Linux. 2. Set `"terminal.integrated.fontFamily": "Iosevka Term"` (or `"Iosevka Fixed"`). 3. Open the integrated terminal. 4. Observe characters rendered too close together and slightly overlapping — only in the terminal, not in the editor. ## Expected Behavior Characters render at the correct monospace cell width, matching how the font looks in other terminal emulators or on macOS. ## Actual Behavior Characters in the integrated terminal are too close together and slightly overlap. The font appears as if the cell width was measured too wide and glyphs are squeezed into a narrower space. ## Workarounds (both confirmed to fix the issue) 1. Set `"terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration": "off"` in user settings. 2. Set `"disable-hardware-acceleration": true` in `argv.json`. ## Additonal Notes - Affects both **Iosevka Term** and **Iosevka Fixed** — the Fixed variant has no double-width glyphs at all (`fc-scan` reports `spacing: 100`, identical to JetBrains Mono), so font metadata is not the cause. - **JetBrains Mono** renders correctly with `gpuAcceleration` on, under otherwise identical conditions. - The editor text (non-terminal) renders correctly regardless. - Disabling `gpuAcceleration` fully resolves the rendering. - `window.devicePixelRatio`: 1 (no fractional scaling) - Display scaling: 100% - Wayland or X11: Wayland The issue is reproducible with stock release TTFs from the Iosevka GitHub releases page; no custom build plan is required. I opened an issue in the Ioveska repo as well, but it seems likely this is a VSCode issue. - https://github.com/be5invis/Iosevka/issues/3218

title: Local stdio MCP: first tool call after reload can fail with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "invoke")'
description:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Unknown

- VS Code Version: 1.124.2
- OS Version: Windows
- MCP server type: local stdio MCP server

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Reload VS Code
2. Open `MCP: List Servers`
3. Note the local stdio MCP server is shown as `Stopped`
4. Invoke a tool from that server through Chat (do not manually start the server)

Observed behavior:

- The first tool call against the local stdio MCP server can fail with an error such as:
  `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'invoke')`
- Retrying the same tool call immediately succeeds.
- If the MCP server is manually started from `MCP: List Servers` before the first call, the first tool call succeeds.
- An extension-backed MCP server in the same environment does not show this failure pattern.

Expected behavior:

- If VS Code supports start-on-first-use for local MCP servers, the first tool call should wait for startup and succeed, or
- If the server is not ready, VS Code should present a clear MCP startup/ready error instead of failing the tool invocation path.

Additional observations:

- The failure is intermittent but appears on the first call after reload when the local stdio MCP server is in the `Stopped` state.
- Retrying the same call succeeds, which suggests a race/initialization/timing issue in the start-on-demand path for local stdio MCP servers.


Reproducibility:

- Intermittent on the first call after reload; retry usually succeeds immediately.

Relevant environment/notes:

- VS Code version and OS are listed above.
- The problem appears specific to local stdio MCP start-on-demand; extension-backed MCP servers do not show the same pattern.

Example mcp.json
{
  "servers": {
    "mytool": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "${workspaceFolder}/.venv/Scripts/python",
      "args": ["-m", "mytool.mcp_server"],
      "cwd": "${workspaceFolder}"
    }
  }
}

title: Focus moves to static option list items but no visible focus indicator is present:A11y_VisualStudioCode_Improved UI for MCP elicitation_Keyboard
description:
## GitHub Tags
#A11yTCS;#Visual Studio Code Client; #SH_Integrated browser features_Win32_JUNE2026;#DesktopApp;#FTP;#Win32;#A11ySev2;#A11yMAS;#WCAG2.4.3;  #ES Chat_Deeplink;

## Issue Subcategory 
Static content in tab order 

## User Experience 
Static content, such as text, headings, and static labels, is focusable via the Tab key, making it take extra Tab presses to reach actual interactive controls. 

## Repro Steps 
Open VS Code > Trigger an elicitation form in copilot chat > Observe the issue: Focus moves to static option list items but no visible focus indicator is present.

## Actual Result 
When navigating through the elicitation form using the keyboard, focus moves to the static option list items (e.g., multi-select list options). However, there is no visible focus indicator on the focused item. As a result, keyboard users are unable to visually identify which option currently has focus.

## Expected Result 
Focus should move to selectable list item instead of static list within the elicitation form, a clear and visible focus indicator should be displayed. The focused item should be distinguishable from other items using visual cues such as outline, border, or highlighting.

## How to Fix 
Remove tabindex="0" from non-interactive elements; if content needs to be programmatically focused (e.g., for focus management), use tabindex="-1" instead so it is not in the natural tab order. 

## Environment details 
Application Name: VS Code 
VS Code version: 1.124.2
Edition Windows 11 Enterprise
Version 25H2
OS build 26200.8390

title: Agents Window Tabs: Editor Tab settings no longer work
description:
In VS Code, we have around 15 settings that control how editor tabs are rendered. Many of these settings no longer work in the Agents Window. As a result, users who have customized their tab settings may encounter broken tab layouts or behavior that differs from their expectations when they switch to the Agents Window.

Please review these settings and decide which ones should be supported in the Agents Window and which ones should not. For settings that are not supported, it is possible to force a specific value and make the setting read-only within the Agents Window.

Keep in mind that the fewer tab-related settings are supported, the less familiar the Agents Window will feel to users who have customized their VS Code Editor experience.

I tested some of the settings, these are broken:
- `workbench.editor.wrapTabs`: Tabs do not wrap when enabled
- `workbench.editor.showTabs`: The tab bar height is changing when switching between `multiple` and `single`. It should not move, the entire editor layout relies on the tab bar height being `35px` (without compact mode enabled)
- `workbench.editor.pinnedTabSizing` & `workbench.editor.tabSizing`: When set to `shrink` or `fixed` a weird shadow renders on the right hand side of the tab
- `window.density.editorTabHeight`: When set to `compact` the tab height does not change as expected, but the editor layout breaks because it's not expecting that it's getting more space even though it does not.
- `workbench.editor.titleScrollbarVisibility`: the tab bar no longer scrolls so this settings no longer makes sense and should be made read-only

There are more settings which are relevant which I have not tested, check in the settings editor under `workbench tab`

title: Webview resource cache grows unboundedly: media-preview cache-busts with Date.now(), service worker never evicts (21+ GB observed)
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes
(media-preview and the webview service worker are built-in, so `--disable-extensions` does not affect the leak.)

- VS Code Version: 1.123.2 (commit 3c631b164c239e7aeaaae7c626b46c527b361af2, x64)
- OS Version: Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (also observed under WSL Remote – Ubuntu)

## Summary

`%APPDATA%\Code\WebStorage\<n>\CacheStorage` grew to **23.5 GB** on my machine.
I parsed the Chromium simple-cache entry keys to find out why. The root cause is a
combination of two pieces of built-in code:

1. **media-preview cache-busts with the current time, not the file version.**
   `extensions/media-preview/src/imagePreview/index.ts` (`getResourcePath`) appends
   `?version=${Date.now()}` on **every render**. Every time an image is opened or
   re-rendered, the URL is brand new — even if the file is unchanged.

2. **The webview service worker caches every response and never evicts.**
   `src/vs/workbench/contrib/webview/browser/pre/service-worker.js` does
   `cache.put(event.request, ...)` for every 200 response with an ETag, keyed by the
   full URL including the query string. The file contains no eviction, expiry, or
   quota logic. The `activate` handler doesn't even delete caches from previous
   `VERSION`s — my disk holds both `vscode-resource-cache-4` (2.09 GB) and
   `vscode-resource-cache-5` (21.38 GB).

Combined effect: **every view of an image permanently writes a full copy to disk**,
and each copy is dead on arrival — the `Date.now()` query string guarantees no future
request can ever hit it.

## Evidence (from parsing the cache entry keys)

My 21.38 GB cache origin contains 6,413 entries:

- They map to only **1,947 unique files** (1,013 files cached ≥ 2 times).
- The most-viewed image was cached **86 times within a single hour** (one evening,
  up to 9 copies in one minute) — per-render, not per-modification.
- In a sample of the 200 most-duplicated paths, **81% point to files that no longer
  exist** on disk.
- Zero video/audio entries: `<video>` uses Range requests (206), which the SW marks
  `no-store` and the Cache API cannot store anyway. The leak therefore only bites
  image-heavy workflows and grows slowly enough to evade detection — which is
  presumably why earlier reports (#131226, #166632 [145 GB], #152519 [500 GB]) died
  as "cannot reproduce" / stale.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Note the size of `%APPDATA%\Code\WebStorage` (`du -sh ~/.config/Code/WebStorage` on Linux).
2. Launch `code --disable-extensions` and open a large PNG (e.g. 20 MB) in the
   built-in image preview.
3. Close the tab and reopen the same file 10 times.
4. The folder grows by ~10 × the image size. None of the new entries can ever be
   read back (each was stored under a unique `?version=<timestamp>` URL), and they
   are never cleaned up.

## Expected

Either of:
- media-preview keys the cache-busting parameter on the file's mtime instead of
  `Date.now()`, so unchanged files reuse one cache entry; and/or
- the service worker evicts stale versions of the same base URL when caching a new
  one, applies an LRU/size cap to `vscode-resource-cache-*`, and deletes
  previous-`VERSION` caches on activate.

## Related

#131226 (closed as stale, "needs repro"), #166632 (145 GB, closed as duplicate),
#152519 (500 GB, closed as duplicate), #310384 (open, 30 GB via Remote-SSH — same
mechanism; this report adds the root-cause analysis).

title: Copilot SDK mutates shared extension host process.env (GIT_CONFIG_*=safe.bareRepository=explicit), breaking git for other extensions — Flutter iOS builds fail with "xcodebuild encountered an error (74)"
description:
<!-- Filed here because the dedicated microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat repo was archived 2026-05-20 (read-only); the built-in extension's package.json lists microsoft/vscode in its bugs.url. -->

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No

<!-- The built-in GitHub Copilot Chat extension is itself the cause; disabling all extensions removes it and the problem disappears. -->

- VS Code Version: 1.122.1 (8761a5560cfd, arm64)
- OS Version: macOS 26.4 (Apple Silicon)
- Built-in GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.50.1 / bundled @github/copilot SDK 1.0.49
- Also involved: Dart-Code + Flutter iOS build (SwiftPM), Xcode 26.5

## Summary

The `@github/copilot` SDK bundled inside the **built-in** Copilot Chat extension mutates the **shared extension host's** `process.env` to inject git hardening config (`safe.bareRepository=explicit`). Every child process spawned by *any other extension* afterwards inherits it, breaking any tool that operates on bare git repos. It broke **all Flutter iOS device builds launched from VS Code** with a misleading error, costing ~3 hours to diagnose:

```
Failed to build iOS app
Could not build the precompiled application for the device.
Uncategorized (Xcode): xcodebuild encountered an error (74)
```

Terminal `flutter run` and Xcode both work fine — only VS Code launches fail, because only the extension-host environment is poisoned.

## Root cause (from the shipped bundle)

`extensions/copilot/node_modules/@github/copilot/sdk/index.js`, de-minified:

```js
function bHt() {
  let count = parseInt(process.env.GIT_CONFIG_COUNT || "0", 10);
  // ... returns early if already present ...
  process.env.GIT_CONFIG_COUNT = String(count + 1);
  process.env[`GIT_CONFIG_KEY_${count}`] = "safe.bareRepository";
  process.env[`GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_${count}`] = "explicit";
}
```

This writes to the **global `process.env` of the shared extension host**, not to the env of Copilot's own child processes.

## Evidence of cross-extension contamination

The Flutter daemon spawned by the (unrelated) Dart extension inherits the injection:

```
$ ps eww <flutter-daemon-pid> | tr ' ' '\n' | grep GIT_
GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit
GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1
```

The VS Code main process and the extension host show **no** such variables at spawn time — confirming the mutation happens at runtime, after Copilot activates. It's also racy: a Flutter daemon spawned *before* Copilot activates is clean, so the failure is intermittent across windows/sessions.

## Why it breaks SwiftPM / Flutter iOS builds

SwiftPM stores repository caches as **bare** repos (`~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm/repositories/`). With `safe.bareRepository=explicit` injected via env, every git call xcodebuild/SwiftPM makes against those caches dies:

```
fatal: cannot use bare repository '.../org.swift.swiftpm/repositories/firebase-ios-sdk-...' (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')
xcodebuild: error: Could not resolve package dependencies
→ "xcodebuild encountered an error (74)"
```

A user-level `git config --global safe.bareRepository all` **cannot** fix this — env-injected config outranks global config. Users have no clean way to defend themselves.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Flutter project with SwiftPM-based iOS deps (e.g. Firebase) in VS Code with the built-in Copilot Chat active.
2. Hit Run / F5 targeting a physical iOS device (or run the minimal repro below).
3. Build fails with `xcodebuild encountered an error (74)`. Terminal `flutter run` and Xcode succeed.

Minimal repro of the poisoned git call (no Flutter needed):

```
cd ~/Library/Caches/org.swift.swiftpm/repositories/<any>/
GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.bareRepository GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=explicit git fetch
# → fatal: cannot use bare repository ...
git fetch
# → works fine
```

## Expected behavior

Copilot's git hardening should be scoped to the env passed to **its own child processes** (`spawn(cmd, { env: { ...process.env, GIT_CONFIG_* } })`), never written into the shared extension host's global `process.env`. The host is shared by all extensions; mutating its env contaminates unrelated products.

## Workarounds (for others hitting this)

- Dart/Flutter: add `"dart.env": { "GIT_CONFIG_COUNT": "0" }` to settings, then Reload Window; or
- `"chat.disableAIFeatures": true` to disable the built-in Copilot entirely.

description:

**Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?:** Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
<!-- Bug Report -->



- **VS Code Version:** 1.124.0
- **OS Version:** macOS 14.7.7 (Sonoma), iMac (Late 2013, Intel Core i5, 24 GB RAM)
  - Note: this machine runs Sonoma via OpenCore Legacy Patcher. However, the behavior described below is reproducible from source-level logic that is platform-independent (see Root cause), so it is not specific to this hardware or to macOS.

## Summary

When previewing a standalone `.html` file in the Integrated Browser **without any folder/workspace open** (empty window), the preview is blocked with:

> `Forbidden. File does not reside within a trusted folder.`

This happens **even when Workspace Trust is fully disabled**, with the following user settings:

```json
{
  "security.workspace.trust.enabled": false,
  "security.workspace.trust.untrustedFiles": "open",
  "security.workspace.trust.emptyWindow": true
}
```

Setting `security.workspace.trust.enabled: false` is an explicit declaration that the user trusts all local content. The editor honors this (files open without any prompt), but the Integrated Browser's `file://` handler does not, which is inconsistent. Rendering a file in the sandboxed browser view is arguably a weaker operation than opening it in the editor with full extension/task capabilities, yet only the former is blocked.

Additionally, because the **Workspaces: Manage Workspace Trust** command is hidden when `security.workspace.trust.enabled` is `false` (its precondition requires the setting to be `true`), the user has **no discoverable way to fix the 403**: the only UI that could add a trusted folder is unreachable in exactly the configuration that triggers the problem.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Set `"security.workspace.trust.enabled": false` in user settings.
2. Open a new empty VS Code window (no folder/workspace).
3. Open any local `.html` file (`File > Open...`). It opens in the editor without any trust prompt, as expected.
4. Preview it in the Integrated Browser (e.g. **Show Preview** in the editor title bar, or navigate to the `file://` URL in the browser tab).
5. The browser renders: `Forbidden. File does not reside within a trusted folder.` (HTTP 403).
6. Try to add the folder as trusted: `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P` → "Manage Workspace Trust" — the command does not appear, because Workspace Trust is disabled.

## Expected Behavior

With `security.workspace.trust.enabled: false`, `file://` navigation in the Integrated Browser should be allowed (the user has globally opted out of the trust model), or at minimum the empty-window trust settings (`security.workspace.trust.emptyWindow`, `untrustedFiles: "open"`) should be honored.

## Root Cause (from source)

The 403 is returned by the `file://` protocol handler in
`src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserSession.ts`:

```ts
this.electronSession.protocol.handle(Schemas.file, request => {
    const filePath = normalize(URI.parse(request.url).fsPath);
    if (!BrowserSession._trustedFileRoots.findSubstr(filePath)) {
        return new Response(localize('browserSession.untrustedFile',
            'Forbidden. File does not reside within a trusted folder.'), { status: 403 });
    }
    ...
});
```

`_trustedFileRoots` is populated by `sendTrustedFileRoots()` in
`src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/browserViewWorkbenchService.ts`, which only considers:

1. the current workspace folders (if `isWorkspaceTrusted()`), and
2. `workspaceTrustManagementService.getTrustedUris()` (the persisted "Trusted Folders & Workspaces" list).

The `security.workspace.trust.enabled` flag is never consulted in this computation. In an empty window there are no workspace folders (so #1 contributes nothing regardless of `emptyWindow: true`), and a user who has had trust disabled has an empty trusted-URI list (so #2 is empty). The result is an empty root set and an unconditional 403 for every `file://` URL.

So the two trust systems are disconnected: the workbench short-circuits to "everything trusted" when the feature is disabled, but the browserView trust-roots computation has no concept of that state.

## Workaround (confirmed)

1. Temporarily set `"security.workspace.trust.enabled": true` and reload.
2. Run **Workspaces: Manage Workspace Trust** → "Trusted Folders & Workspaces" → **Add Folder** → add a parent folder of the HTML files (e.g. the user home directory).
3. Set the setting back to `false` and reload.

The persisted trusted-URI list (`content.trust.model.key`, application storage) is loaded unconditionally by `getTrustedUris()`, so the preview keeps working afterwards. This confirms the mechanism, but it relies on undocumented behavior and requires toggling a security setting just to reach the relevant UI.

## Suggested Fix

In `sendTrustedFileRoots()`, when `workspaceTrustEnablementService.isWorkspaceTrustEnabled()` is `false`, either treat all local files as trusted (consistent with how the rest of the workbench behaves in that state), or honor the empty-window trust result for the file roots as well.

### Issue
When configuring a Custom Endpoint in the VS Code model configuration (BYOK scenario), the `apiKey` is currently injected as an `Authorization` header using the value `Bearer <apiKey>`. However, this is not consistent, since the apiKey is not a Bearer token.

**Expected Behavior**
- The header name should either be configurable, or
- The value specified as `apiKey` in the configuration should be sent as an `api-key` header, not as a `Bearer` token in `Authorization`.

### Steps to Reproduce:
1. Configure a model with a Custom Endpoint in VS Code with an `apiKey`.
2. Observe the outgoing request headers.

### Impact
This behavior may cause authentication/authorization errors for services that expect the API key in a custom header (e.g., `api-key`) rather than in the bearer token format.

title: VS Code Doesn't Show "Use Workspace Version" for TypeScript in Multi-Root Workspaces or  in Monorepo Setup
description:
# VS Code Workspace Uses Bundled TypeScript Instead of Project TypeScript in Multi-Root Workspace

## Description

When working in a multi-root VS Code workspace, TypeScript language features appear to use VS Code's bundled TypeScript version instead of the TypeScript version installed in the project that owns the currently open file.

This causes diagnostics to differ between:

* Opening the project folder directly
* Opening the same project inside a multi-root workspace

## Workspace Structure

```text
xxx-system-workspace
├── xxx-laravel-api-phase-two
└── xxx-next-js-phase-two
    ├── package.json
    ├── tsconfig.json
    └── node_modules/typescript
```

The Laravel project does not use TypeScript.

The Next.js project contains:

```json
{
  "devDependencies": {
    "typescript": "^5"
  }
}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a multi-root workspace containing:

   * A Laravel project
   * A Next.js project with TypeScript installed locally

2. Open the `.code-workspace` file in VS Code.

3. Open a `.tsx` file inside the Next.js project.

4. Run:

```
TypeScript: Go to Project Configuration
```

VS Code correctly opens the Next.js project's `tsconfig.json`.

5. Run:

```
TypeScript: Select TypeScript Version
```

VS Code offers:

```
Use VS Code's Version 6.0.0-dev
```

and appears to use bundled TypeScript diagnostics instead of the project's installed TypeScript version.

## Expected Behavior

Since VS Code correctly identifies the owning `tsconfig.json`, it should automatically use the TypeScript SDK installed in the owning project:

```
xxx-next-js-phase-two/node_modules/typescript
```

or at minimum clearly expose the workspace version associated with that project.

## Actual Behavior

VS Code appears to prefer the bundled TypeScript version for language features when opened through a multi-root workspace.

As a result:

* Diagnostics differ from project builds.
* Diagnostics differ from opening the Next.js folder directly.
* TypeScript behavior changes depending on whether the project is opened standalone or as part of a workspace.

## Additional Notes

Opening only the Next.js folder causes VS Code to correctly use the project's TypeScript version and the issue disappears.

This suggests the problem is related to TypeScript SDK resolution within multi-root workspaces rather than project configuration.

title: Block auto-approval of file-write redirection to ~ and % paths
description:
Extends the file-write redirection guard to also block auto-approval when the destination path contains `~` (POSIX tilde expansion) or `%` (Windows env-var expansion), since neither `posix.isAbsolute` nor `win32.isAbsolute` classifies these as absolute paths.

Adds regression tests for both bash (`~/file.txt`, `%HOME%/file.txt`) and pwsh (`~\file.txt`, `%APPDATA%\file.txt`).

Tracking internal PR: devdiv-microsoft/vscode-private#43

title: Copilot Chat: ADO auth-change handler re-fetches semanticsearchstatus on every event (missing session-id dedup)
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
 Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No

 <!-- The code lives in the bundled `copilot` extension (`extensions/copilot/` in this repo). -->

 - VS Code Version: 1.123.0 (system setup)
 - OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200

 Steps to Reproduce:

 1. Open VS Code with a workspace containing 2+ Azure DevOps repositories.
 2. Sign in via the Microsoft auth provider.
 3. Wait for all repos to reach `Ready`.
 4. Switch focus to another window and back (or open a new chat turn).
 5. In Dev Tools → Network, observe: one `GET …/semanticsearchstatus` request fires per ADO repo, every time, even though the repos are already `Ready`.

 **Expected:** No re-fetch when nothing changed.
 **Actual:** N requests per event per user, indefinitely.

 ### Root cause

 In `extensions/copilot/src/platform/workspaceChunkSearch/node/codeSearch/codeSearchChunkSearch.ts`, the **GitHub** auth-change handler already dedupes no-op events by comparing session ids (lines 175–188). The **ADO** handler (lines 190–195) doesn't - it fires `updateRepoStatuses('ado', …)` on every event regardless of whether anything actually changed.

 ### Suggested fix

 Apply the same session-id dedup that GitHub already has. Sketch:

 ```ts
 // codeSearchChunkSearch.ts, replace lines 190-195
 {
     let lastAdoSessionId = this._authenticationService.anyAdoSession?.id;
     this._register(Event.any(
         this._authenticationService.onDidAdoAuthenticationChange,
         this._adoCodeSearchService.onDidChangeIndexState
     )(() => {
         const adoSessionId = this._authenticationService.anyAdoSession?.id;
         if (adoSessionId === lastAdoSessionId) {
             return;
         }
         lastAdoSessionId = adoSessionId;
         this.updateRepoStatuses('ado', new TelemetryCorrelationId('CodeSearchChunkSearch::onDidAdoChange'));
     }));
 }
```
Related to commit https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/9e2a9e36812ae9065a6841702229f41859d064b8 which mapped 401/403 to 'not-authorized' and made NotAuthorized sticky in refreshStatusFromEndpoint. That change stopped the silent retry loop for misconfigured users. This issue covers the remaining steady-state volume from healthy authenticated users, which has the same root pattern - updateRepoStatuses firing even when nothing changed.

(Optional, separate) Bonus improvement

updateRepoStatuses calls refreshStatusFromEndpoint(true, …) (line 1003), which forces a network refresh even for repos already in Ready. Adding a short TTL (e.g., 5–10 min) so Ready is sticky would further reduce request volume, but is a larger change. Happy to file separately if useful.

title: Ollama model context size incorrectly determined
description:
## Environment

- **Copilot Chat Extension Version:** 0.41
- **VS Code Version:** 1.123
- **OS Version:** macOS Tahoe 26.5.1
- **Ollama Version:** 0.30.7
- **Feature:** Ollama integration
- **Selected model:** qwen3:4b-instruct

## Error Log

```
Sorry, your request failed. Please try again.

Client Request Id: 8b6a0a1a-fefa-4d2c-9ea1-e20779384434

Reason: Request Failed: 400 {"error":{"message":"{"error":{"code":400,"message":"request (26528 tokens) exceeds the available context size (16384 tokens), try increasing it","type":"exceed_context_size_error","n_prompt_tokens":26528,"n_ctx":16384}}","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":null}} : Error: Request Failed: 400 {"error":{"message":"{"error":{"code":400,"message":"request (26528 tokens) exceeds the available context size (16384 tokens), try increasing it","type":"exceed_context_size_error","n_prompt_tokens":26528,"n_ctx":16384}}","type":"invalid_request_error","param":null,"code":null}}

at bG._provideLanguageModelResponse (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1710:13930)
at processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:104:5)
at bG.provideLanguageModelResponse (/Applications/Visual Studio Code.app/Contents/Resources/app/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:1710:14933)
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Ollama
2. Download a local model (e.g. `qwen3:4b-instruct`)
3. Set the context length in Ollama settings (e.g. 16k)
4. Add Ollama as a model provider in VS Code
5. Select the downloaded model and write a prompt

## Expected Behavior

VS Code should respect the context size configured in Ollama and only send requests that fit within that limit.

## Actual Behavior

VS Code displays the maximum theoretical context size of the model (262k for `qwen3:4b-instruct`) instead of the value configured in Ollama. As a result, VS Code attempts to send requests that exceed the model's actual available context window, causing the request to fail.

## Workaround Attempted

Tried creating a custom model via a Modelfile with an explicit `num_ctx` parameter:

```
FROM qwen3:4b-instruct
PARAMETER num_ctx 16384
```

Run with:

```
ollama create qwen3:4b-instruct-16k -f Modelfile
```

VS Code still displayed 262k as the available context size, ignoring the configured value.

## Additional Context

Setting the context size to 16k in Ollama is necessary because my hardware does not support larger context windows. This makes the mismatch between the displayed and actual context size a real-world issue, not just a cosmetic one — VS Code may attempt to send requests that exceed what the model can actually handle, leading to repeated request failures.

title: Enterprise Policy language file invalid (.adml)
description: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No - VS Code Version: VSCode-win32-x64-1.123.0 - OS Version: Not applicable ## Steps to Reproduce: 1. Download ZIP based installer 2. Sign-in into Microsoft Intune and try uploading the `VSCode.admx` and `en-us\VSCode.adml` files 3. Receive error message ## Solution per GitHub Copilot: I’m checking the ADML structure against the matching ADMX and the XML rules that Intune enforces, so I can identify the exact validation point rather than guess. I’m locating the owning ADMX references for this language file and checking for any schema mismatch or missing resource IDs, which is the cheapest way to falsify whether the issue is just “bad XML” versus a real ADMX/ADML contract break. Search complete: Inspect ADMX linkage Searched codebase for "VSCode.admx VSCode.adml policy schema mismatches Intune validation", no results Searched codebase for "ADMX ADML string and presentation ID references missing or mismatched", no results Searched for files matching `**/VSCode.admx`, 1 match Searched for files matching `**/VSCode.adml`, 14 matches Searched for regex `VSCode.admx|VSCode.adml`, no results Searched for regex `en-us|en_US|PresentationId|StringId` (`**/*.admx`), no results Searched for regex `Category|PolicyDefinition|Policy|Resource` (`**/*.admx`), 133 results Searched for regex ` Plugin enablement. Keys are plugin IDs in `@` form; ... ... Git URIs (`[#ref]`). ``` In XML text, ``, ``, and `` are parsed as child elements, not literal text. That makes the document malformed unless they are escaped as `<plugin>`, `<marketplace>`, and `<url>`. Intune validates the ADML as XML first, so it will reject the file before it even checks whether the ADMX/ADML references line up. The fix is to escape those angle brackets in every affected ADML locale. For the English file, the two values should read roughly like this: ```xml ... IDs in `<plugin>@<marketplace>` form ... ... Git URIs (`<url>[#ref]`) ... ``` I did not see a matching ADMX/ADML ID mismatch in the portion I checked; the parser error is the strong root-cause candidate here. If you want, I can patch all affected ADML files in this policy set. ## Results After manually patching the `.adml` file I was able to upload it into Intune.

title: VSCode seems it does not respect my profiles when starting some extensions
description:
Type: Bug Hello there, I recently posted a similar issue for new Agents window. In that task I explained that I disabled many features in the "Default" profile, including all AI, and the profile I am starting agent window is fully decorated for AI works. Yet, agents window tries to use "Default" profile to connect agents, and fails miserably to do so becuause of changes I made to "Default" profile. The same is now happenning with Remote Explorer. I also removed Remote Explorer from "Default" profile. And now I am not able to connect WSL containers, and vscode complains saying "Extension 'WSL' is required. And it says this after I started this connection from within Remote Explorer, just from another profile set for this purpose. How can you recreate the issue? follow these steps: 1- Open "Default" profile and remove WSL, and maybe Remote Explorer(?!) 2- Create a new profile, from scratch or using default 3- switch to new profile, find and install WSL 4- open Remote explorer window and try to connect a WSL container (current or new windows, wont matter) 5- Now witness: VSCode switches to "Default" profile immediately before trying to connect, and it fails because there is no WSL in "Default" profile. 6- Bonus: open File menu, and then "Close Remote Connection". The profile stays in "Default". One exception I saw so far is this: If I enable WSL in "Default" profile, open a remote folder, and switch to another profile that has WSL enabled within that folder, then next time I try to connect from non-Default profile, it reopens the folder in that profile without a problem. Everything I use in VSCode should be contained within the profile I am working in. The exception clearly shows that my profiles are respected in the workspace level, but not in global level. I hope you fix this issue and bring balance and peace to the use of profiles.
